_overview.lead_en: 圆明园 Yuanmingyuan was not one palace but a great number of compounds, halls, courts and small gardens set round lakes and hills: 212 compounds in our inventory. Every scene and compound outside the European palaces now has a dossier: what it was, the album leaf of 1744 where there is one, how it changed before October 1860, its halls one by one, what survives, and what is known of its size, each figure with how it was got.
_overview.how_en: The ten best-documented scenes have a page of their own; the others are summarised below and open in the 3D view with all their evidence. Most sizes come from the Qing plan and from the Yangshi Lei drawings, a few from excavations. On the plan, the names at 九洲清晏 are those of the Tongzhi repair of 1873, not of 1860.
_overview.lead_zh: 圆明园不是一座宫殿，而是环绕湖山布置的殿宇、庭院与园林，我们的清单中共有212组。西洋楼以外的每一景、每一组建筑现在都有一份专题资料：概况，1744年四十景图（如有），1860年10月以前的变化，逐座建筑，现存遗迹，以及已知尺寸和每个数字的得出方法。
_overview.how_zh: 资料最丰富的十景另有专页；其余各景列于下方，可在三维视图中查看全部证据。尺寸多来自清代地盘图和样式雷图档，少数来自考古发掘。地盘图上九洲清晏一带的名称属同治十二年（1873年）重修，并非1860年的状况。

YM03.what_en: 九洲清晏 Jiuzhou Qingyan, "Nine Continents Clear and Calm", is the largest of the nine islands round the Back Lake 后湖 Hou Hu and the emperor's residence from Yongzheng to Xianfeng (S05 j80:20b-23b; E1129; S02 pp.77-79, E1153; E1134). Its central axis runs from the Front Lake 前湖 Qian Hu north through three halls: 圆明园殿 Yuanming Yuan Dian (five bays, the garden's name plaque in Kangxi's hand), 奉三无私殿 Fengsan Wusi Dian (seven bays) and 九洲清晏殿 Jiuzhou Qingyan Dian (seven bays in S05; a Yangshi Lei record gives five bays with a three-bay rear porch, S310 rec. 7237), whose plaque is in Yongzheng's hand. East of the last stands 天地一家春 Tiandi Yijia Chun, west 乐安和 Le'anhe (so named as the sleeping hall in 1774) and further west 清晖阁 Qinghui Ge with small buildings round a court (S05 j80:20b-21a, 24a-25b). Malone found the island so built up that there was room for almost no artificial hills (E1153). A fire on 丙申九月二十六日 (1836) burned the three axis halls; Daoguang rebuilt them in under a year to the old form, adding nothing, by his own account (御製重修圓明園三殿記) (E1131, E1132, E1134). 慎德堂 Shende Tang on the west side was built in 1831, the date of Daoguang's essay for it (E1130; S310 rec. 7342); 同道堂 Tongdao Tang had a theatre by 1855 (S43). On 7 October 1860 Swinhoe walked through the audience hall to the emperor's bedroom, where the treaty of 1858 lay on a table (S02 pp.180-181, E2111). Malone, citing Favier, reports that fires broke out during the looting of 6-8 October and burned the emperor's own residence, before the ordered burning (S02 p.183, E1151). The burning of 18-19 October by British troops on Elgin's order followed (E0485). Tongzhi's repair of 1873 renamed several halls (E1135, Q36).
YM03.scene_en: Leaf 3 of the 1744 album (P0003). Qianlong's preface (S40, E1091; printed in S05 j80:23b-24a) opens: '正大光明直北為㡬餘游息之所棼橑紛接鱗瓦參差前臨巨湖' ('straight north of Zhengda Guangming is the place to rest from affairs; rafters crowd together, scaled tiles stand uneven, and in front lies a great lake'). He compares the islands round the lake to Zou Yan's nine continents ringed by the great ocean, then recalls his father living here, working at maps and books, and binds himself to the same diligence: the poem lists the fear of Heaven and of the people, and sets the fine dishes of the kitchen against the hungry in the ditches. The preface and poem are moral rather than descriptive: they give the dense roofs and the lake in front, not a layout.
YM03.later_en:
The 日下旧闻考 Rixia Jiuwen Kao (S05 j80, compiled after 1774) adds what the album lacks: by 1765 the tall pines before 清晖阁 had burned and Qianlong set small buildings round its court, a two-storey 松云楼 Songyun Lou on the high ground of the stone wall, 露香斋 Luxiang Zhai by a rockery, 涵德书屋 Hande Shuwu and the book room 茹古堂 Rugu Tang (j80:24a-25a, E1094). In 1774 Qianlong named the sleeping hall 乐安和; his note says the room he had lived in before was called 随安堂 Sui'an Tang (j80:25a-b, E1099). Jiaqing wrote on 九洲清晏, 奉三无私 and the small studios (E1106-E1114); Daoguang built 慎德堂 in 1831 (E1130) and, after the fire of 1836, rebuilt the three axis halls by 1837 (E1134). The theatre at 同道堂 dates to 1855 at the latest (S43). The plan S01 shows the island after Tongzhi's renaming of 1873 and carries a pasted slip for a later rearrangement (E1135, E1152, Q36); the Yangshi Lei drawings E1156-E1171 record the 慎德堂 interiors and the 九洲清晏 axis at several dates.

Yangshi Lei sheets give three states of the island. Before the fire of 1836: 样004-5 九洲清晏旧样 and 样005-4 慎德堂 fit-out (E1171, E1156). After it: 样005-34 of 1837, an unapproved first round, and 样010-3, the approved rebuilding, which gave the west side of the 九洲清晏 hall the 同道堂 annex instead of a mirror of the east (E1169). Xianfeng: 样007-9-1 of 1855.3 for 圆明园殿 (E1163), 样005-13 and 样005-27-1 of 1855.9, for a three-bay rear porch added to the 九洲清晏 hall that year (E1162), 样004-2-1 for the hall and 同道堂 (E1170), and 样011-3 九洲清晏全样 of 1855.10-12, the latest whole-scene plan found before 1860 (E1161); and the 慎德堂 interior sheets of 1851, 1856 and 1859, one of the 1859 sheets dated only by the site (E1160, E1174, E1164, E1165). The 1874 plan 故1299 (E1166) is Tongzhi's design: same three axes and most old names, but a jade-disc pond with a double-eaved square pavilion between 奉三无私 and 天地一家春, a seven-bay hall north of it, 慎德堂 as five bays under four roofs, 思顺堂 in the west court (S310 rec. 11901). The 1873-74 three-garden plan 样1203 renames 基福堂 to 同顺堂 and 天地一家春 to 承恩堂 (E0532; S310 rec. 7217); the decree of 1873, as quoted in S220, has 思顺堂 for 基福堂 (E1135). S01's labels here (七间殿, 福寿仁恩, ?顺堂, 承恩堂, 同顺堂) are those of the Tongzhi design, which supports Q36.
YM03.interior_en: Plaques and couplets by hall (S05 j80:21a-23a): 圆明园殿 has Kangxi's 圆明园 plaque, a couplet Yongzheng wrote as a prince ('每對青山緑水㑹心處…') and one by Qianlong; 奉三无私殿 holds Qianlong's copies of the moral instructions of Kangxi and Yongzheng, the plaque 清虚静泰 and a couplet at the throne; 九洲清晏殿 carries Yongzheng's plaque in front and 蔚然深秀 at the back. On the north wall of 清晖阁 hung the painted map of the whole garden of 1737 by Castiglione, 唐岱 Tang Dai, 孙祐 Sun You, 沈源 Shen Yuan, 张万邦 Zhang Wanbang and 丁观鹏 Ding Guanpeng, inscribed 大观 (j80:23a; S02 p.62). In 1860 Swinhoe found, in what he took for the emperor's own rooms, a moderate room with a double-seated throne, chandelier and clocks, two small rooms and a spiral stair to two upper rooms of books whose windows looked down into the hall (E1037); M'Ghee a court about 50 ft square flagged in marble and the only spiral stair, on the left, in the ladies' rooms (E1150). Hérisson's side rooms full of gold, beside the throne hall, are not trusted (S246 pp.315-317, E2441).
YM03.setting_en: The island faces the Front Lake on the south and the Back Lake on the north (S05 j80:20b, 23b; E1153). Malone found little rockwork and almost no artificial hills on it (E1153). In the west court a long stone wall stood opposite 清晖阁, with tall pines in front that had burned by 1765 and others still standing outside the wall; 露香斋 sat by a rockery with real trees (S05 j80:24a-b). M'Ghee describes the apartments' front on 'another sheet of water' with large planted rockeries (E1150); Wolseley and Swinhoe reached them by a pebbled path round half a pond from behind the audience hall (E1037, E1038). Bridges: 如意桥 Ruyi Qiao on the south-east and 南大桥 Nan Da Qiao on the south-west, 棕亭桥 Zongting Qiao at the north-west corner (S313; S41).
YM03.survives_en: The island keeps its shape between the front and back lakes. An archaeological survey (勘探) report gives the scene about 220 x 120 m, 25,000 m2, with 8,600 m2 of buildings and 656 rooms and gallery bays (S151, opening only); a 紫禁城 article of 2011 gives the island about 234 x 116 m and 21,600 m2 (S313). The page that carries the report says that the foundations of the Tongzhi repair were wrecked in 1900 by bannermen and bandits (S151); who did the damage of 1900 is disputed (Q28). No dig report with hall sizes has been seen; the paywalled report and a 慎德堂 dig record are on the wish list.
YM03.best_en:
For the 1860 state the plan to get is 样011-3 九洲清晏全样 (1855.10-12, NLC; 1207x675 mm, ink, light colour, yellow slips; E1161), with 样005-27-1 (rear porch of 1855) and 样007-9-1 (圆明园殿 measured 1855.3, its slips give bays, depth, column height and platform). For interiors 样008-18 (1859.7) is the latest dated 慎德堂 state found. None of these images could be seen: mhymy shows only the catalogue header and an introduction (where some slip figures are transcribed); the full record is behind a reply wall or payment. The 1874 plans (故1299, 样1203) and the 烫样 are of the Tongzhi repair and must not replace the 1855 sheets.

The 1744 leaf (P0003) is the period colour record of the island's axis before the 1836 fire: grey tile throughout, red columns with green-blue lattice, three main halls rising north from the front lake, stepped covered galleries between them, dense courts east of the axis and pines west. Bays are only roughly countable at the 1920 px copy. The 1745 woodcut (P0089) draws the courts more fully and adds a pyramid-roofed pavilion on the hill at top left; the 1887 page (P0234) is a re-cut of it. The gouache (P0103) recolours roofs yellow and is not evidence for colour. (S08 P0003; S76 P0089; S260 P0234; S77 P0103)
YM03.gaps_en: For the axis halls S05 gives bays only. The 1855 slips of 样007-9-1, read in the mhymy transcription only, give bays, depth, column height and platform for 圆明园殿 (S310 rec. 11195); for the other halls no depth, roof form, storeys or tiles were found in any text read. The 1855 overall plan E1161 and the interior drawings of 慎德堂 (E1156-E1160) are research-only and their sizes were not read here. 怡情书史, 基福堂, 同道堂 and the 1855 theatre have no Qing text of their own in this round beyond the 1873 renaming (E1135). The S360 compilation of dated records could not be fetched again this round (site timed out).
YM03.what_zh: 九洲清晏是后湖周围九岛中最大的一座，自雍正至咸丰为皇帝寝居之所（S05 j80:20b-23b；E1129；E1153）。中轴自前湖向北依次为圆明园殿（五间，悬康熙御书“圆明园”匾）、奉三无私殿（七间）和九洲清晏殿（《日下旧闻考》记为七楹，样式雷档案记为五间接后抱厦三间，S310），东为天地一家春，西为乐安和，再西为清晖阁（S05 j80:20b-25b）。道光十一年（1831）建慎德堂（E1130）。道光十六年（1836）失火，三殿被焚，道光帝命照旧制重修，不到一年完工（E1134）。1860年10月6日至8日英法联军进园抢掠；马龙（Malone）引樊国梁（Favier）称，皇帝寝宫在抢掠期间已经起火（E1151）。10月18日至19日，英军奉额尔金之命焚烧圆明园（E0485）。同治十二年（1873）重修时，岛上多座殿宇改名（E1135，Q36）。
YM03.survives_zh: 岛形尚存，位于前湖与后湖之间。考古勘探报告（仅见开头）称该景区东西约220米、南北约120米，占地约25000平方米，建筑面积约8600平方米，殿宇、游廊共656间（S151）；《紫禁城》2011年一文称全岛东西约234米、南北约116米，约21600平方米（S313）。登载报告的网页称，同治重修的基址在1900年被旗兵和土匪破坏（S151）；1900年的破坏者为谁仍有争议（Q28）。目前未见载有单体殿宇尺寸的发掘报告。
YM03.summary_en: The emperor's residence: the largest island of the Back Lake, three halls on one axis north of the audience hall, rebuilt after the fire of 1836 and burned in October 1860 (E1153; E1134; E0485). Its 1855 state is known from Yangshi Lei plans not yet seen in full; the base plan here carries names of 1873 (E1161; Q36).
YM03.scene_zh: 《圆明园四十景图》第三幅（P0003）。乾隆帝诗序开头说：“正大光明直北為㡬餘游息之所棼橑紛接鱗瓦參差前臨巨湖”，又以邹衍九州环以大瀛海之说比喻湖中诸岛（S40；E1091）。诗中追念父皇在此“左图右书”、勤于政务，并以“六膳八珍”对照沟壑中的饥民以自警。序与诗重在训诫，不记布局。
YM03.summary_zh: 九洲清晏是后湖最大的岛，皇帝寝居之所，三殿沿中轴排列，1836年火后重修，1860年10月被毁（E1153；E1134；E0485）。

YM01.what_en: 正大光明 Zhengda Guangming, "Upright and Bright", is the audience hall Yongzheng built in the south of the garden to hear government (構殿于園之南御以聴政) after his accession in 1723 (S05 j80:2b; Malone dates it 1725, S02). Visitors passed the spirit wall (Malone: 137 ft long), the Front Lake 前湖 Qian Hu on both sides of the road, the five-bay 大宫门 Da Gongmen with five-bay offices before it and the boards' duty rooms behind (S05 j80:7b-9a, E0999, E2101; E2114), then three stone bridges over a moon-shaped canal to the second gate 出入贤良门 Churu Xianliang Men (five bays), where military officers and guards were presented and archery was shot; duty rooms stood either side, with the kitchens to the south-west and the Grand Council 军机处 Junji Chu to the south-east (j80:9a-b, E1000). Inside stood the seven-bay hall with five-bay side halls, 寿山殿 Shoushan Dian behind and 洞明堂 Dongming Tang to the east (j80:9b). It served for audiences, New Year banquets, examinations and birthday congratulations into the 1850s: Mongol princes feasted here on the fifteenth of the first month (S202 j15, E1182), palace re-examinations of new graduates were held here from 1844 to 1849 (S202 j9, E1023), and Xianfeng received congratulations here in 1852 (S207, E1557). French troops reached the gardens on 6 October 1860 and British troops on 7 October, and the hall was looted with the rest in the days to 8 October (S02 pp.179-183; E2111, E2113). During the burning of 18-19 October, ordered by Elgin, British troops were quartered at the hall and set it alight last, about three in the afternoon of 19 October (M'Ghee p.288, E1028; S02 p.77, E1007).
YM01.scene_en: Leaf 1 of the 1744 album (P0001). Qianlong's preface (S40, E0995; S05 j80:11a) calls the hall the formal court of the garden, '不雕不繪得松軒茅殿意' ('uncarved and unpainted, it keeps the sense of a pine lodge and a thatched hall'), with a steep rock wall behind it like jade shoots, an open forecourt, and flowering trees beyond the walls in layers of red and purple. The poem ties the hall to the model of 畅春园 Changchun Yuan, praises thrift, and notes in a gloss that the plaque of 出入贤良门 is in his father's hand.
YM01.later_en:
The plain hall of 1744 was dressed up later: a terrace 月台 with four censers was added between 1775 and 1793 (S119, params.json), and by the end of Qianlong's reign, Malone writes, the columns were red, with dragon capitals and gilt wire over the frieze (S02 pp.75-76, E1009), though Barrow saw no capitals in 1793 (E1026). Macartney's gifts were set up in the hall in 1793 (S02 p.76, E1008; Barrow E1026) and the Dutch embassy was received here in 1795 (E1007). Jiaqing let Han officials of the first two ranks into the Mongol princes' New Year banquet from 1802 (S202 j15, E1182) and moved the re-examination of successful clansmen here from 1814 (E1022); Daoguang moved the palace re-examination of new graduates here from 1844 (E1023). In 1801 the 南书房 Nan Shufang, the Southern Study, got a four-bay room near the Council office (S202 j4, E2124). By 1860 a large painting of the gardens hung on the left (west) wall as one entered, where S05 records a 豳风图 Binfeng tu (S05 j80:10b; E1030, E1031).

Only one Yangshi Lei sheet of the hall was found open: 样001-4 正大光明白差准底 (NLC, undated, 520x210 mm). Its figures, read in the mhymy transcription, give the bays: central 1丈6尺1寸5, next two 1丈5尺1寸, four end bays 1丈3尺5寸, verandas 6尺, 金柱 depth 3丈8尺, so seven bays of about 32.1 m plus verandas, about 36 x 16 m overall (1 尺 = 0.32 m); the rear veranda walled in, verandas on three sides, ten door-screen sets front and back, a throne canopy 7尺4寸 x 1丈2尺 at the back of the central bay (S310 rec. 10451; E1016). The record says the verandas on three sides agree with the 1744 leaf (P0001). The 初编 holds pp.13-31 on 正大光明 (E1015), not seen.
YM01.interior_en: S05 j80:10b: Yongzheng's couplet '心天之心而宵衣旰食 樂民之樂以和性怡情', Qianlong's couplet '遹求寜觀成無逺弗届 以對時育物有那其居', the 無逸 Wuyi chapter on the east wall and a 豳风图 on the west. Barrow (1793) measured the room 110 x 42 ft and 20 ft high, with a ceiling painted in circles, squares and polygons, a grey marble floor, two rows of columns, red pillars at the throne recess and a throne of wood like mahogany (E1026); Macartney saw windows on one side only and the throne opposite (E1008). In 1860 the witnesses describe a polished marble floor, a carved throne on a low dais with three flights of steps (Swinhoe found it lesser wood painted as ebony), books in yellow silk, enamel bowls and French clocks, and a great painting of the gardens on the left wall, or at one end in M'Ghee (Swinhoe pp.294-295, E2105, E1030; Wolseley pp.234-235, E1031, E1032; M'Ghee p.204, E1029; Varin pp.232-233, E2122). Hérisson's carved ironwood columns and yellow tiles stand alone and are not trusted (E1027).
YM01.setting_en: Behind the hall rose 寿山 Shou Shan, a steep rock hill (屋後峭石壁立玉筍嶙峋, S40 in S05 j80:11a, E0995), with pines and a rockery (S02, E1009); behind that a pond crossed by a pebbled path and bridge on the way to the island of 九洲清晏 (Swinhoe pp.296-298, E1037; Wolseley pp.235-236, E1038). The court of the 大宫门 had guard-houses on three sides, carved and roofed with coloured tiles, with small beasts on the eaves in red, white, green, blue and gilt (Wolseley pp.231-232, E2109); the hall stood at the far side of a long flagged court, with a wire net under its eaves against birds (Wolseley pp.232-233, E1033; Swinhoe, E2105). A pair of large bronze lions stood on pedestals on either side of the road to the gate (Wolseley, E2123; Varin, who gives white marble pedestals, E2122). The road from the spirit wall ran between the two halves of the Front Lake to the gate (S05 j80:7b, E0999; E2114).
YM01.survives_en: The site of the audience hall is open lawn today, with a few stones in rows, and the rocky hill 寿山 Shoushan behind it still stands (P0363); the front lake 前湖 keeps a low stone edge (P0396). A survey report describes three courts from 大宫门 Da Gongmen to 正大光明殿, 370 m from north to south (S102, E1017). The dig at 大宫门, one of the campaigns since 2012, found the gate hall, its east and west wing gates, the 金水桥 bridge and the channel, and the area was to be conserved and shown (E0363, S132, E2120).
YM01.best_en: P0001 shows the south front plainly: the curved moat with red railings, a flat white bridge on the axis (only one visible, against three in the text, j80:9b), 出入贤良门 with its wings, the paved court, 正大光明殿 of about seven bays on a stepped platform, the tall blue-grey rock peaks of 寿山 among pines behind it, and walled office courts west and east. The woodcut P0100 and its 1887 re-cut P0232 repeat the layout; the gouache P0102 paints the roofs green. (S08 P0001; S05 j80:9b, j80:11a)
YM01.gaps_en: Apart from 样001-4, read only in the mhymy transcription (S310 rec. 10451), no Qing text read gives a size in 丈尺 for any hall of 正大光明 or 勤政亲贤 Qinzheng Qinxian; Barrow's inside figures (E1026) and Malone's foundation (E1009) are the other measures. S211 says the bridge before 出入贤良门 was bow-backed and was levelled in 己亥 (1839), so in 1860 it was flat; the 1744 leaf already draws a flat bridge, and S05 gives three bridges where S211 speaks of one, so neither settles its form before 1839. The date the 豳风图 on the west wall gave way to the painting of the gardens the 1860 witnesses saw is unknown.
YM01.what_zh: 正大光明殿是雍正帝即位（1723）后在园南所建的听政正殿，“構殿于園之南御以聴政”（S05 j80:2b）；马龙（Malone）定为1725年（S02）。自影壁北行，辇道两侧为前湖，经五间大宫门（门前东西朝房各五间，门后为各部院直房，E2101），再过月牙形河上的三座石桥，至五间二宫门出入贤良门，武职侍卫在此引见、较射，西南为茶膳房，东南为军机处（S05 j80:9a-b；E1000）。门内为七间正大光明殿，东西配殿各五间，后为寿山殿，东为洞明堂。此殿用于朝会、正月筵宴、考试和庆贺，直到咸丰年间（E1182；E1023；E1557）。1860年10月6日至8日英法联军进园抢掠（S02 pp.179-183）；10月18日至19日英军奉额尔金之命焚园，英军驻扎于此殿，19日下午约三时最后将其焚毁（E1028；E1007）。
YM01.survives_zh: 正大光明殿遗址今为草地，残存成行石块，殿后寿山假山尚存（P0363）；前湖保留低矮石岸（P0396）。勘探报告称自大宫门至正大光明殿为三进院落，南北长370米（S102，E1017）。2012年以来的发掘中，大宫门遗址发现门殿、东西配门、金水桥及河道，计划保护展示（E0363，S132，E2120）。
YM01.summary_en: The garden's audience hall at the head of the south axis, behind the Great Palace Gate and the gate 出入贤良门: a plain seven-bay hall used for audiences, banquets and examinations into the 1850s (E1000; E1023; E1557). Looted with the rest on 6-8 October 1860; troops had been quartered in it and the lodges before it, so these were among the last buildings the British troops burned, on 19 October (E2111; E1028).
YM01.scene_zh: 《圆明园四十景图》第一幅（P0001）。乾隆帝诗序称此殿为园中正衙，“不雕不繪得松軒茅殿意”，殿后峭石壁立如玉笋，前庭虚敞，墙外花木红紫层叠（S40；E0995）。诗中以畅春园为规范，倡导节俭，并注明出入贤良门匾额为其父雍正帝所书。
YM01.summary_zh: 正大光明殿是圆明园南部中轴上的听政正殿，1860年10月6日至8日遭英法联军抢掠；因军队曾驻扎于殿内及其前的值房，这些建筑是英军最后焚毁的一批，时在10月19日（E1000；E2111；E1028）。

YM02.en: Diligent in Government and Friendly with Officials
YM02.what_en: 勤政亲贤 Qinzheng Qinxian is the working court east of the audience hall: the five-bay 勤政殿, where the emperor read memorials and saw officials until noon (S05 j80:11b, 17b-18a; E1066, E1039), and east of it a cluster of small halls, a pavilion and courts: 飞云轩, 静鉴阁, 怀清芬, 秀木佳荫, 生秋庭, 芳碧丛, the three-bay 保合太和殿, the storeyed 富春楼 and 竹林清响 (j80:19a-20a, E1067). Malone calls it a smaller audience hall with adjacent courts (S02 p.77, E1082). It stayed in daily use to the end: audiences in the hall in summer and in the east study in spring and autumn (S211, E1088), and Xianfeng kept mourning for his father in 飞云轩 in 1850 (S207, E1089). It burned in October 1860 with the core of the garden; S50 says the gate and three courts of the neighbouring 吉祥所 survived (E1083, a lead).
YM02.scene_en: Leaf 2 of the 1744 album (P0002). Qianlong's preface (S40, E1039; S05 j80:17b-18a): east of the audience hall is 勤政殿, '日於此披省章奏召對臣工亭午始退' ('daily here I read memorials and summon officials, leaving only at noon'), with the 無逸 written on the screen behind the seat; further east 保合太和 among fine rocks and flowers, bright courts, linked pavilions and paths through trees. The poem is a pledge of diligence: no rest by day or night, every word weighed.
YM02.later_en:
Qianlong added to the plaque 为君难 a colophon and poems of 1759 and 1785, Jiaqing a poem of 1801 and Daoguang a note of 1823 (S360, E1072); the court is listed among the scenes whose later plans differ from the album (S41; the rule in research/questions.md under Q1), so S01 wins on layout. No dated rebuilding was found in the texts read.

Sheets: 样002-3 踏勘勤政殿东书房尺寸底 of 咸丰五年三月 1855 (E1084), figures behind the paywall; 样002-17 保合太和 (undated), whose slip gives three bays of 3丈6尺 and 2 x 3丈2尺 (32.0 m), depth 3丈6尺, a three-bay front porch 2丈2尺 deep, columns 1丈4尺: each bay subdivided into three on the facade, so it reads as nine (S310 rec. 10368). 勤政殿 itself: five bays with three-bay 抱厦 front and back (S310 rec. 7310). Lei family 烫样 of 勤政殿 exist, of the Tongzhi repair (S920).
YM02.interior_en: S05 j80:12a-b and 19b-20a list the fittings: the plaque 勤政亲贤 and the rear plaque 为君难 by Yongzheng, Qianlong's couplets front and rear, the 无逸 on the throne screen, and on the rear walls Qianlong's two essays on ruling written out by 梁诗正 (east) and 于敏中 (west); in 保合太和殿 the Four Admonitions on the wall and plaques in the west warm room; in 富春楼 four plaques downstairs. S211 adds the working arrangement: three bays of folding doors opened, a partition front and back, an east study without a porch with its door to the east (E1088).

YM41.what_en: 大宫门 Da Gongmen, the Great Palace Gate, is the south front of the garden and the start of the official axis to 正大光明 (S05 j80:7b-9a, E2101). From the spirit wall (Malone: 137 ft long, about 15 ft high, E2114; the dig report gives 41.6 m, 204.8 m south of the gate, S102 E1017) the carriage road ran north between the two halves of the Front Lake to the five-bay gate hall, with five-bay court offices left and right before it (S05 j80:7b-8b). Behind the court offices stood the duty rooms of the boards and the eight banners, east and west by name, the silver vault and 南书房 in the east lane and the 造办处 workshop and dispensary in the south-west (j80:8b-9a). The gate carried Yongzheng's plaque 圆明园 (j80:1b; Malone says Kangxi's: question row). The three courts from the gate to the hall measure 370 m north-south and 310 m between the 如意门 gates by the dig report (E1017). Amherst reached the gate at daybreak in 1816 and left without an audience (S02, E2112). On 6 October 1860 French troops with a British cavalry brigade arrived at seven in the evening, and a few eunuchs defended the gate (S02 from Cordier, E2110); the looting followed on 7-8 October. The dig of the late 2010s found the gate hall, the east and west wing gates, the 金水桥 and the canal (S132, E2120).
YM41.setting_en: Wolseley saw ponds with lilies and lotus at the edges along the causeway, a temple under tall trees at its end, and gate courts enclosed on three sides by carved and painted guard-houses whose sills stood 2-3 ft above the pavement with granite ramps (S240, E2108; pp.231-232, E2109). Lucy describes a small lake and wood on the left of the approach and the great gate at the back of a vast half circle (S247, E2103). A Daoguang-era Manchu account has yellow earth spread on the road and side streets curtained as the emperor rode by (S02 from 鸿雪因缘图记, E2116).
YM41.survives_en: The 大宫门 area was dug by the 北京市文物研究所 in at least two phases (a 2016 request of the 北京市文物局 says the second was finished, per a search extract of S154; results announced January 2019): gate hall, east and west wing gates, the 金水桥 and the river (S132; S154). The gate hall stood on a base 21.57 x 11.33 m, 0.77 m high; the screen wall is 41.6 m long and 204.8 m south of the gate terrace (S102 as recorded in E1017). The 12-page brief (S154) is locked.
YM41.gaps_en: No plan of the 大宫门 itself found. The wall plans 样098-3 (1811-27) and 样1704 write wall lengths (E0530, E0529); the 初编 section 正大光明 pp.13-31 (E1015) may include the gate.

YM32.en: Paradise Island of the Enameled Green Terrace
YM32.what_en: 蓬岛瑶台 Pengdao Yaotai, "Paradise Island of the Enameled Green Terrace", stands on three islands in the middle of 福海 Fuhai (S05 j82:16b, E1933). The central island has a three-bay gate facing south, a seven-bay main hall, 畅襟楼 Changjin Lou and 神洲三岛 Shenzhou Sandao before it to the east and west, and 随安室 Sui'an Shi and 日日平安报好音 on the east and west sides (S05 j82:16b, E1933); a bridge south-east leads to the east island with the pavilion 瀛海仙山 Yinghai Xianshan, a bridge north-west to the north island with a three-bay hall (j82:16b). Under Yongzheng it was called 蓬莱洲 Penglai Zhou; the new name dates from 1744 (S05 j80:10a, j82:16b). Malone: a small palace court with glazed tile on the central island, the north-west island also built over, the east island a rustic retreat with pavilion, rocks and trees (S02 p.93, E1936). On the dragon-boat day under Qianlong the emperor sat in the pavilion 望瀛洲 Wang Yingzhou and the empress dowager watched the race from 蓬岛瑶台, east of it (S202 j14, E1889). A list drawn from 刘敦桢 Liu Dunzhen (1933) puts 蓬岛瑶台 among the seventeen or so places where buildings still stood after the burning of 1860 (E0451); when they were lost is not stated in the texts read.
YM32.scene_en: Leaf 32 of the 1744 album (P0032). Qianlong's preface (S40, E1925; S05 j82:17a): '福海中作大小三島仿李思訓畫意為仙山樓閣之狀' ('in the Sea of Blessings three islands, large and small, were made, after the paintings of 李思训 Li Sixun, as towers of the immortals on their peaks'), looking like the 'five golden halls and twelve jade towers'. He adds that large and small are one: know this, and here are the sacred isles, and one may boil rivers and mountains in a half-pint pot. The poem gives famous flowers, white jade steps, and 'towers and halls in the water, steeped in 琉璃' (水中樓閣浸琉璃), 琉璃 being both glaze and glass-clear water.
YM32.later_en: The dragon-boat feast moved from 望瀛洲 and 蓬岛瑶台 to 澄虚榭 Chengxu Xie under Jiaqing; the race was still held in the early Daoguang years and then stopped (S202 j14, E1889). S360 files 28 dated items under 福海, 1741-1858, 26 of them poems, on boating, the view and the summer heat (E2365): the lake was in use to the end. No dated rebuilding was found in the texts read.
YM32.setting_en: On P0032 the main island carries a yellow-roofed gate with green-tiled wings on a stone base and a white stair to the water, the main hall behind with a blue upper roof trimmed in yellow and a purple-brown lower roof, a green-roofed two-storey 楼 on the east and a railed terrace on the west; the north-west islet is grey-tiled behind white walls and linked by an arched timber bridge; the east islet carries a hexagonal pavilion among willows. Rocks edge every shore. (S08 P0032)
YM32.survives_en: The islands of 蓬岛瑶台 survive in 福海 Fuhai, whose shape is kept (S146, S148). Modern structures stand on them: seen from the shore, a glazed pyramidal pavilion roof and a white-walled hall with a grey roof on a rock base (P0791, P0387). No excavation report of the islands was found (S946).
YM32.gaps_en: No Yangshi Lei drawing or card model of 蓬岛瑶台 was found: none on the mhymy list of c. 150 records (walked page by page), none in two searches. The 初编 目录 in the catalogue (S13) lists no 蓬岛瑶台 section; it may sit in the 续编 or under 福海. Positions rest on S01 and the 1744 leaf. When the buildings that stood after 1860 were lost, and what remains on the islands today, is not on disk.
YM32.what_zh: 蓬岛瑶台位于福海中央，由三座岛屿组成（S05 j82:16b, E1933）。中岛有南向宫门三楹、正殿七楹，殿前东为畅襟楼、西为神洲三岛，东偏为随安室，西偏为日日平安报好音；东南过桥为东岛，有亭名瀛海仙山；西北过桥为北岛，有正宇三楹（E1933）。雍正时名蓬莱洲，乾隆九年（1744）改今名（S05 j80:10a）。乾隆年间端午，皇帝在望瀛洲观龙舟，皇太后则在其东的蓬岛瑶台观竞渡（S202 j14, E1889）。据刘敦桢1933年的史料整理，1860年焚园之后此处仍有建筑留存（E0451），其后何时毁失，现有资料未载。
YM32.survives_zh: 蓬岛瑶台诸岛仍在福海之中，福海保持原有轮廓（S146，S148）。岛上今有新建建筑：从岸上可见一座琉璃攒尖亭顶，以及一座建在石基上的白墙灰瓦殿宇（P0791，P0387）。未见诸岛的考古发掘报告（S946）。
YM32.role_en: The Three Islands in the Happy Sea
YM32.summary_en: Three islands in the middle of the Fuhai lake, built as the isles of the immortals after the paintings of Li Sixun, with a court of glazed halls on the central island. Buildings still stood here after the burning of 1860.
YM32.scene_zh: 四十景图第三十二景（P0032）。乾隆帝诗序云：“福海中作大小三島仿李思訓畫意為仙山樓閣之狀”，望之若“金堂五所玉樓十二”；又言小大一如，能知此理，则此即三壶仙岛（S40, E1925; S05 j82:17a）。诗中写名花、白玉墀，以及“水中樓閣浸琉璃”。
YM32.summary_zh: 福海中央的三座岛屿，仿李思训画意营造为仙山楼阁，中岛为琉璃瓦宫殿院落；1860年焚园后仍有建筑留存。

YM54.what_en: 福海 Fu Hai, the Sea of Blessings, also called the East Lake 东湖, is the largest water of the garden, 'some qing round' (周廣凡數頃, S05 j82:14a), roughly square and almost half a mile a side by Malone, joined by a narrow opening to the lake before 方壶胜境 (S02 p.93, E2370). Eight of the Forty Scenes stand on its shores and islands (scenes 30-37, E2370): 澡身浴德 in the south-west corner with 澄虚榭 facing east, 望瀛洲 north of it, 平湖秋月 in the north-west corner, 接秀山房 on the east facing west, 别有洞天, 夹镜鸣琴, 涵虚朗鉴 on the east, 蓬岛瑶台 in the middle (S05 j82:14a-22a). Yongzheng took princes and ministers boating and fishing here on festival days (S205, E2364); under Qianlong the dragon-boat race was held on it with painted boats and music, the emperor in 望瀛洲, his mother on 蓬岛瑶台 (S205 E2363; S202 j14, E1889). Attiret describes boats for air, fishing and water jousts, and fireworks and illuminations on the water (E2368). In October 1860 the minister in charge 文丰 Wen Feng is said to have drowned himself in one of the lakes after the gate fell (S02 p.185, E2369).
YM54.setting_en: Attiret saw an island palace on a rock about six feet above the water, quays of stone or rockwork, palaces in tiers and groves round the shore, aviaries half in the water and a fish reservoir closed with brass wire (S157, E2366, E2367). The 1744 prefaces give low ridges and green islets (接秀山房: 平岡縈迴碧沚停蓄), 'bamboo isles and reed banks' with ducks and herons (澡身浴德: 竹嶼蘆汀 ... 浴鳬飛鷺), and the Western Hills seen across the water (S05 j82:14b, 18a).

YM29.en: Elevated Region of the Square Pot
YM29.what_en: 方壶胜境 Fanghu Shengjing, "Elevated Region of the Square Pot", named after 方壶, one of the three isles of the immortals (E1842), stands on terraces near the north-east corner of the 圆明园 proper (S02 p.63), on a lake whose south side opens into 福海 Fuhai by a narrow channel (S02 p.93, E2370). East of 四宜书屋 Siyi Shuwu, on the water, stands a five-bay front building of two storeys with two archways south of it; behind it the storeyed 哕鸾殿 Huiluan Dian and further north 琼华楼 Qionghua Lou; 蕊珠宫 Ruizhu Gong east of 哕鸾殿, with a boathouse south of it and a 龙王庙 behind (S05 j82:12a-13a, E1847). Malone: on the upper brick-faced terrace two large and four smaller two-storey buildings linked at upper level, on the lower terrace by the lake three two-storey buildings, and a bridge and two piers to three small terraces with open pavilions (S02 pp.92-93, E1850). Malone reads the poem's "twelve golden halls" as twelve buildings roofed in golden glazed tile (S02 p.93; E1842); the album leaf shows roofs of several colours (P0029). Its halls were lost when the gardens were burned by British troops on Elgin's order on 18-19 October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188, on the gardens as a whole); its brick and stone stood as a ruin until much of it was pulled down for building material under the Republic (S02 p.218). The outline of the terrace is mapped as a ruin today (S03).
YM29.scene_en: Leaf 29 of the 1744 album (P0029). Qianlong's preface (S40, E1842; S05 j82:13a): sailors never reach the three sacred isles, '要知金銀為宫闕亦何異人寰即境即仙自在我室何事逺求' ('know that palaces of gold and silver are no different from the human world; the place itself is the immortals' land, here in my own house: why seek far'); 蕊珠宫 lies east and 三潭印月 Santan Yinyue on clear water to the west. The poem opens with 'flying towers drawn into the clouds, the mirror water holding them' (飛觀圖雲鏡水涵) and pines and cypresses reaching the sky.
YM29.later_en: Plans: 样042-2 方壶胜境北路 (NLC, 637x562 mm, ink and light colour, presentation sheet, late Daoguang; E1855) and the elevation sheet of the copper dragon and phoenix (E1856, shown at the NLC 典籍博物馆, no catalogue data). The record lists the twenty gilt-copper plaques written in 乾隆五年三月 (1740) and hung that tenth month: 迎薰亭, 集瑞亭, 凝祥亭, 宜春殿, 锦绮楼, 翡翠楼, 哕鸾殿, 碧云楼, 紫霞楼, 琼华楼, 千祥阁, 万福阁, 芝田日永, 阆苑春深, 麐舞灵台, 凤鸣珠树, 蕊珠宫, 依仁殿, 履义殿, 蕊珠门 (S310 rec. 8298). The site's modern introduction gives the scene as 160 m north-south by 125 m east-west, 20,000 m2 of ground and 7,000 m2 of buildings, begun about 1738 (S310 rec. 8298, no survey stated; it may count 三潭印月 and 天宇空明 in the extent); Malone dates the palace 1740 (S02 p.93). Figures of 样042-2 are not in the free part.
YM29.interior_en: Plaques by S05 j82:12b-13a: the scene plaque in Qianlong's hand; on the upper storey of the front building 宜春殿 and 敬胜怠; on the archways 芝田日永 and 阆苑春深 (south faces), 凤鸣珠树 and 鹿寿灵台 (north faces; the 1740 list in S310 has 麐舞灵台); on 哕鸾殿's upper storey 用厥中 and 有真赏在; 琼华楼 漱芳润. A Yangshi Lei elevation sheet of its bronze dragons and phoenixes (方壶胜境铜龙、凤立样底图) is known by title (E1856, research-only).
YM29.setting_en:
Malone: the main buildings on a large square terrace faced with brick, 'In the courtyards stood pines, magnolias, incense burners, and other ornaments and trees'; a lower terrace on the lake to the south; a central bridge and two piers to three small terraces with open pavilions and marble balustrades, with steps down to the water for the imperial barge; a smaller palace on the shore east of the terrace, another across the lake to the north, pavilions, a boathouse and ornamental rocks on the hills and shores round (S02 pp.92-93, E1850). The 1744 poem adds pines and cypresses 'reaching the sky' and a high ridge (S05 j82:13a, E1842). Malone dates the palace 1740 (p.93, note to the 圆明园则例).

P0029 shows 方壶胜境 standing on white stone terraces in the water: three double-eaved pavilions in front (yellow in the centre, blue at the sides), a two-storey front range, a middle court with bronze vessels, and a rear range with a blue double-eaved centre; all columns and lattice red, roofs glazed in yellow, purple-brown, blue and green; a climbing gallery on the west hill and a long grey boathouse on the east shore (S08 P0029).
YM29.survives_en: The stepped stone platform survives at the lake edge: dressed stone bastions project into the water at different lengths, with broken marble blocks stacked on them (P0383, P0787, P0788). Under the Republic the gardens' ruins were quarried for stone and brick (S02 p.218). No excavation report of this scene was found (S946).
YM29.what_zh: 方壶胜境以海上三神山之一“方壶”为名（E1842），位于圆明园东北部（S02 p.63），其前湖南端以狭窄水口与福海相通（S02 p.93）。据《日下旧闻考》，四宜书屋之东临池楼宇为方壶胜境，上下各五楹，南建坊座二；其北楼宇为哕鸾殿，又北为琼华楼；哕鸾殿东为蕊珠宫，宫南有船坞，后有龙王庙（S05 j82:12a-13a, E1847）。Malone（1934）记其主体建于砖砌方台之上，台上楼阁皆二层，以飞廊相连，台前临湖另有三座二层楼和三座伸入湖中的石台（S02 pp.92-93）。乾隆五年（1740）御书铜镀金字匾二十面（S310）。1860年10月18日至19日英军奉额尔金之命焚园，此处殿宇亦毁（S02 pp.187-188）；民国时期残存的砖石遗构又多被拆运（S02 p.218）。今存台基遗址（S03）。
YM29.survives_zh: 方壶胜境临水的阶梯状石台基尚存：长短不一的条石台墩伸入水中，上面堆放着残破的汉白玉构件（P0383，P0787，P0788）。民国时期园中遗址曾被拆取石料和砖（S02 p.218）。未见此景的考古发掘报告（S946）。
YM29.summary_en: The most elaborate palace of the Yuanming Yuan proper, built about 1740 on brick-faced terraces by a lake off the Fuhai, with storeyed halls under glazed roofs of several colours. Its halls were lost in 1860 and much of its masonry was pulled down under the Republic.
YM29.scene_zh: 四十景图第二十九景（P0029）。乾隆帝诗序说，海上三神山“舟到風輒引去”，不过妄语；“要知金銀為宫闕亦何異人寰即境即仙自在我室何事逺求”，并记其东为蕊珠宫，西为三潭印月（S40, E1842; S05 j82:13a）。诗首句云“飛觀圖雲鏡水涵”，写楼阁倒映水中、松柏参天。
YM29.summary_zh: 圆明园中最为华丽的一组楼阁，约建于乾隆五年（1740），建在临湖的砖砌高台之上，屋顶覆多色琉璃瓦；1860年被焚，民国时残存砖石又遭拆运。

YM46.en: The Wen Yuan Ko, Library of the Source of Literature
YM46.what_en: 文源阁 Wenyuan Ge, the library that held a set of the 四库全书, stands a little west of north of 水木明瑟, with 柳浪闻莺 to the west (S05 j81:35b-36a, E2195). S05 dates it 乾隆三十九年 (1774) and pairs it with 文渊阁 in the palace and 文津阁 at Chengde (j81:36a). Qianlong's 文源阁记, cut on a stele in a pavilion east of the library, says he took the form of 天一阁, the Fan family library in Zhejiang, whose bay count and beam and column sizes follow the idea 'heaven one gives birth to water' (天一生水) (j81:36b-37a, E2194). It has six bays on each of two floors (j81:35b); the 2024 dig confirms six bays and black glazed roof tiles (E2207, S133). The pierced rock 玲峰 from 大房山 stands in the pool in front (j81:36b-39a). Malone saw the stele still standing and fragments of white-and-green wave-pattern glazed tile (S02 pp.89-90, E2198). The library and its books burned in October 1860 with the garden (E0485).
YM46.scene_en: Not one of the Forty Scenes (built 1774). The texts that stand for the leaf are Qianlong's 文源阁记 and poems in S05 j81:36b-39a: '因輯四庫全書命取其閣式以構庋貯之' ('compiling the Four Treasuries, I ordered its pavilion form taken to build a store for them', E2194); the 1776 poem '天一取閣式 文津實先構' (E2186); and two songs of 1775-76 on the 玲峰 rock, said to surpass the 'eighty-one holes' of Mi Fu's famous stone (E2181, E2185). The library replaced the Yongzheng pavilion 四达亭 (params.json, S134).
YM46.later_en: The only plan of 文源阁 found on mhymy is Tsinghua T0049, dated 光绪二十四年 (1898), a presentation sheet of 1225x700 mm: 38 years after the burning, so a survey or project on the ruin, not the 1860 state (S310 rec. 7842; E2205). The record dates the library to 乾隆四十年 (1775), built on the site of the square double-eaved 四达亭 of 1731, whose inner screens Castiglione painted in 1728. The NLC 文源阁图样 (E2204) remains undated beyond 清末.
YM46.setting_en: A rock garden round a pool: the monolith 玲峰, 'with inscriptions on it and pierced with many holes, rising 12 or 15 feet from a stone terrace in the middle of the pool' (S02 pp.89-90, E2198), with Qianlong's poem cut on it (S05 j81:36b). The 1776 poem speaks of a 月台 and 'strange stones heaped into peaks' (詭石堆竒岫, j81:37b). The dig found two ponds, one before and one east of the library, walls of 虎皮石 rubble, and the base of 玲峰 of long slabs tied with iron dovetails (E2206, E2207).
YM46.survives_en: Before the 2024 dig the library and stele-pavilion platforms were fairly whole, with the gate, steps, a cracked-ice floor and black and green glazed scraps on the ground; the square pond had gone and the 玲峰 rock lay broken in two (S105 sect. 3.2). The 2024 dig (August to November, 北京市考古研究院) found the gate, the north gate, library and stele-pavilion foundations, walls of rubble, flagstone paths, the 玲峰 base, two ponds and five culverts, and confirmed six bays and black glazed tiles (S133; S134; S942). Sizes in metres from the dig are not yet published; the Guangxu 丈尺册 gives the bays (S105 note [4]).
YM46.best_en: No pre-1860 Yangshi Lei plan of 文源阁 was found on mhymy; the Tsinghua plan T0049 is of 1898. The river-and-revetment plan 样043-1 (E0540) shows the 文源阁 court of 1775 at about 1:200 and is the best period plan for its footprint.

YM45.en: She Wei Ch'eng or Wall of Sravasti
YM45.what_en: 舍卫城 Shewei Cheng, named after Sravasti, the Indian city of the Buddha, is a walled Buddhist town at the north end of the 同乐园 shop street, over twin bridges, with three archways before it (S05 j82:27b-28b, E2146; S02 p.94, E2067). On its south face stands 多宝阁, a shrine of 关帝; inside a gate, the main hall 寿国寿民, then 仁慈殿 and 普福宫; 最胜阁 on the north (j82:28a). Malone thinks it the 佛城 'being built at the same time as the Fang Hu Sheng Ching, 1740' after the 圆明园则例, found yellow glazed tile inscribed She Wei Ch'eng and 'made in the 15th year', and describes red-walled temples inside and a gate on the north like the south one (S02 p.94 n.45). Attiret's 'little town' of 1743 with four gates, towers, walls and battlements is identified with it and the street south of it (S157, E2174). Varin, in October 1860, saw walls about 8 m high with a broad raised gallery on top divided into countless niches with gilt bronze statuettes (S245 pp.240-241, E2178), the form that fits 舍卫城. It burned with the garden in October 1860.
YM45.interior_en: Plaques by S05 j82:28a: on the archways 花界 and 香城 (north), ?涌 and 金池 (east), 昙霏 and 珠林 (west); 多宝阁 '至圣大勇' for 关帝; 寿国寿民殿 '心月妙相'; 仁慈殿 '具足圆成'; 普福宫 '瑞应优昙'; the archway at 最胜阁 '乾闼持轮' and '祗林垂鬘'. Varin's 'infinite number of small niches' with gilt bronze statuettes on the wall gallery (E2178) is the only 1860 view inside; his count of statues is his own estimate.
YM45.survives_en: The first season at 舍卫城 (June to December 2019, 500 m2) found the south gate, wall stretches and ramps, the processional road, guard rooms and a culvert. The gate tower base is 15.4 x 12.6 m and stands up to 1.25 m, with a 三合土 core and stone facing; the guard rooms do not sit where the Yangshi Lei drawing puts them (S46; E2180).
YM45.gaps_en: No drawing of 舍卫城 found on the mhymy list or by search. Only typology and S01 for now.

YM44.what_en: 同乐园 Tongle Yuan, 'Garden of Shared Joy', is the court's theatre north of 曲院风荷 Quyuan Fenghe: two storeyed viewing buildings of five bays facing south, the three-tier stage 清音阁 Qingyin Ge facing north, 永日堂 Yongri Tang to the east, and through the middle the North-South Long Street 南北长街 with 抱朴草堂 Baopu Caotang on its west, leading north over twin bridges to 舍卫城 Shewei Cheng (S05 j82:27b-28a, E2146; E2148). It was reached from the Great Palace Gate by going east through the 东楼门 and about a li by boat (S202 j13, E2148). Under Qianlong banquets with plays were held here every year from the thirteenth of the first month for clansmen, Mongol princes, envoys and officials, and on imperial birthdays (E2148); S360 lists 155 dated items, 1738-1860 (E2152). Xianfeng held his birthday feast here in 1852 (S207, E1557). Malone describes a granite road between two rows of buildings, including the theatre, which 'looked like a business street in a city' (S02 p.94, E2067).
YM44.scene_en: Not one of the Forty Scenes: it lies within the view of leaf 38, 坐石临流 Zuoshi Linliu (P0038). Qianlong's preface to that leaf (S05 j82:26a) ends '東為同樂園' after a pavilion over a rocky stream; the poem recalls the orchid-pavilion gathering of 永和. Malone captions the later edition of leaf 38: 'The theater is in the square courtyard at the right. Shops line both sides of the street which leads across a bridge to the gate of She Wei Ch'eng' (S02 p.95).
YM44.later_en: The great stage 清音阁 of 同乐园 is given in metres on mhymy record 7297, converted from a Yangshi Lei drawing that the page does not name: lower central bay 5.50 m, side bays 4.51 m (front c. 14.5 m), platform 0.96 m, middle storey 14.53 m square inside the eaves, upper storey 13.09 m, eave columns 4.42 / 3.71 / 2.72 m, 23.94 m from the ground to the ridge; a plan of 道光十八年 (1838) to cut it to two storeys, 3.60 m lower, met objections from officials; whether it was carried out is not known here (S310 rec. 7297). The National Museum of China holds a card model (烫样) of the 同乐园 group; one report says it was made for Tongzhi's repair (S328, E2158), another gives no date (S922).
YM44.interior_en: S202 j13 (E2148): the emperor and consorts in the five-bay main building, the guests in the east and west wings, each placed in an assigned room; a stage "about ten zhang deep and wide" (some 32 m, against about 14.5 m in the drawing's figures) in three tiers, gods let down from the top and demons up from below; plays with titles such as 清平见喜 and 万年甲子; actors chosen by the textile commissioners (织造), customs superintendents and salt offices until Daoguang sent the 南府 Nanfu players home in 1821 and eunuchs took over. Hanlin officials first sat in under Jiaqing (E2150). Attiret describes the court fair, which Malone places on this street (S02 p.95): eunuchs played the merchants, with quarters for silks and cloth and streets for porcelain and lacquer, and real goods from Peking dealers (S157, E2160).
YM44.survives_en: No dig of 同乐园 has been found. The best figures for the lost buildings are those of the 清音阁 stage converted to metres on 梦回圆明园 Menghui Yuanmingyuan from an unnamed Yangshi Lei drawing (see above; S310, ysltd 7297). The shopping street ran straight for over 130 m north to 舍卫城 (S941).
YM44.what_zh: 同乐园位于曲院风荷以北，是宫廷的戏园：前后楼各五间，南向；其前为北向的三层大戏台清音阁；东为永日堂；中有南北长街，街西为抱朴草堂，街北过双桥即舍卫城（S05 j82:27b-28a；E2146；E2148）。据《养吉斋丛录》，自大宫门东转东楼门，乘舟约一里可到；乾隆年间每年自正月十三日起在此赐宴听戏，宗室王公、蒙古王公和属国陪臣入座，万寿节前后也在此演戏（S202 j13；E2148）。咸丰二年（1852）咸丰帝万寿时仍在此赐宴（S207；E1557）。马龙（Malone）记述，两排房屋夹着花岗石路，其中有戏台，“像城里的商业街”（S02 p.94；E2067）。
YM44.survives_zh: 目前未见同乐园的考古发掘。现有最好的尺寸是梦回圆明园网站据一张未注明的样式雷图换算的清音阁数据（S310，ysltd 7297）。买卖街向北直通舍卫城，长逾130米（S941）。
YM44.summary_en: The court theatre: a three-tier stage facing two five-bay viewing buildings, with the shop street leading north to 舍卫城; banquets and plays were held here from Qianlong to Xianfeng (E2146; E2148; E1557).
YM44.scene_zh: 同乐园不在四十景之内，位于第三十八景坐石临流的范围（P0038）。乾隆帝诗序在写到溪上石亭之后说“東為同樂園”，诗末以东晋永和兰亭修禊作比：“年年上已尋歡處便是當時晉永和”（S05 j82:26a）。
YM44.summary_zh: 同乐园是圆明园的宫廷戏园，有三层大戏台清音阁和通往舍卫城的买卖街，自乾隆至咸丰在此赐宴演戏（E2146；E2148；E1557）。

YM15.what_en: 山高水长 Shangao Shuichang, "Hills High and Waters Long", the open ground in the south-west corner of Yuanming Yuan, south-west of 万方安和. A tower facing west, nine bays, with linked hills behind it, a stream before it and level ground of several qing in the middle (S05 j81:15b; E1519). The editors date the tower to 1726 and give its first name as 引见楼; behind it a rear court with side halls and a landing by a cross pavilion; before it a slanted riding track, an earth target wall to the north-west, and the thirteen courts 十三所 to the south-east that served the firework nights (S361 v2 p.147; E1529). Used from Yongzheng to Xianfeng for the New Year feast of Mongol princes and envoys in great tents, guards' archery, and fireworks at the Lantern Festival (S05; E1519, E1521, E1528, E1535); in 1795 the Dutch embassy was received in a tent here (S02 pp.167-170; E1526). Daoguang reviewed the 精捷营 here in 1839 (E1328, E1346) and Xianfeng shot with guns here in 1855 (E1518). Burned with the garden in October 1860; nothing visible today (E1011).
YM15.scene_en: Leaf 15 of the 1744 album. Qianlong's preface: "在園之西南隅地勢平衍構重樓數楹" (in the south-west corner of the garden, on level ground, a storeyed tower of several bays). He says the far hills and near fields lie open to view, that foreign princes are feasted here at New Year with fish-and-dragon shows and wrestling, and that in ordinary times the guards practise archery. The poem praises the feast as uniting inner and outer peoples ("内外一家連") (S40, printed in S05 j81:18a; E1515).
YM15.later_en:
日下旧闻考 (1780s) adds a horizontal stele at the left bay carrying the edict of 1752, with the edict of 1778 on sparing the bravest soldiers cut on its back (S05 j81:15b-18a; E1519). The 养吉斋丛录 calls the place 西厂, the West Yard, and lists the banquet of the 19th of the first month with wrestlers and acrobats (S202; E1521); 檐曝杂记 describes 3,000 lantern dancers before the tower forming the characters 太平万岁, then fireworks (S213; E1520). Jiaqing set a rain altar here in 1812 (S47 p.118; E1527). Xianfeng's note of 1855 mentions Qianlong's earth wall with a carved poem, used for gun practice (S360 p.145 item 152; E1518). On the 21st day of the 7th month of 咸丰六年 (1856) the Xianfeng emperor came by boat and landed "至山高水长后阁扇下船，出前门", at the rear of the tower, then left by its front gate: the tower had a water landing behind (east) and its gate on the field side (S210; E1524). The Yangshi Lei sheets for this place are mostly 道光-同治 (S13 pp.157-172; E1532), one Qianlong sheet shows seven Mongol tents and the fireworks before the tower (S310 样018-1号; E1535).

Drawings: 样018-4-1, the 山高水长 tower plan of 道光十一年 1831 (presentation sheet with yellow slips and paste-overs, E1534); 样018-1 of the Qianlong reign, the layout of seven Mongol tents and fireworks for the New Year banquets in front of the tower, the largest tent c. 24 m across (E1535); record 7326 is a second plan of the scene without catalogue data (E1533). The field was c. 460 x 280 m per the mhymy record (S310 rec. 7326).
YM15.interior_en: Plaque 山高水长 in Qianlong's hand; the stele at the left bay with the edicts of 1752 and 1778 (S05 j81:15b; E1519). During feasts the emperor sat in a great tent 武帐 set on the field, not in the tower (S337; E1528, E1535). Van Braam (1795) describes the imperial rooms elsewhere as small, neatly furnished, with a few books and curiosities (S02 pp.167-170; E1526); that passage is not about this tower.
YM15.setting_en:
Level grass field, the largest open space in the garden (S02 p.83; E1525), backed on the east by a chain of low hills ("後擁連岡") with a stream in front ("前帶河流") (S05 j81:15b; E1519). Across the stream Malone records a straight horse run of half a mile from a round tower in the north to 藻园 in the south, with a small shrine to General Liu Meng by the round tower (S02 p.83; E1525). An earth target wall to the north-west (E1529, E1518). On feast days Mongol tents and firework frames stood on the field (E1535, E1520).

P0015 shows the open field closed by low wooded hills, with the long two-storey 山高水长楼 seen end-on from the south: a 卷棚歇山 roof, a grey brick gable wall below, wood-coloured lattice along the upper storey and no red columns; a chain of small grey courts runs south-east of it. No tents or targets are drawn. (S08 P0015, crop ym15_c1)
YM15.gaps_en: The 1831 tower plan 样018-4-1 and the Qianlong tent layout 样018-1 are both open on mhymy only as catalogue headers and an intro; their slip figures are not.

YM20.what_en: 澹泊宁静 Danbo Ningjing, "Placid and Calm", is the rice-field scene east and a little south of 日天琳宇 Ritian Linyu: paddies all round, ringed by water, with at the centre a hall on the plan of the character 田, four gates, and towers on its east and north sides; the north tower's main room bears the name (S05 j81:29a; E1633). It stood by 1727 (S361 v2 p.182; E1640; S310 rec. 2579). West of it, in a separate wall, stood the seven-bay 多稼轩 Duojia Xuan facing south and a group of farm-themed halls, named in ten poems of 1759 and repaired in 1760 (S05 j81:30b-33b; E1620; E1647); the S361 editors file this group under the next scene, 映水兰香 Yingshui Lanxiang (S361 v2 p.185; E1670). Qianlong watched the harvest from 稻香亭 Daoxiang Ting here (E1651, E1652). It was burned by British troops on 18-19 October 1860 (E0485); digs of 2020-2022 exposed the whole base of the 田字房 Tianzi Fang, with heavy burning on base, courts and paths that the excavators link to that fire (S137; S139; E1643, E1644).
YM20.scene_en: Leaf 20 of the 1744 album (P0020). Qianlong's preface: "仿田字為房密室周遮塵氛不到" (rooms built on the character 田, close rooms walled round, where the dust of the world does not reach). Outside are pagoda-tree shade and trailing flowers, rippling water, reeds; the name comes from Zhuge Liang's maxim 澹泊以明志 宁静以致远, to which the poem points as "武侯妙語" (S40, printed in S05 j81:30a-30b; E1618; the maxim itself opens Jiaqing's poem of 1804, E1628).
YM20.later_en:
日下旧闻考 lists the full group in the 1780s: 曙光楼 east, 翠扶楼 outside the east gate, the western court with 多稼轩, 观稼轩 on the paddy side, 怡情悦目 behind, 稻香亭, 溪山不尽, 兰溪隐玉, 水精域 south of the west pool, 静香屋, 招鹤磴, 寸碧 and 引胜, and 互妙楼 to the north (S05 j81:29a-29b; E1633). The 多稼轩 was repaired in 1760 ("结构年深稍葺治 栋宇从新", S361 v2 p.190; E1647). Jiaqing wrote on 澹泊宁静 in 1804 and 1807 (E1628, E1631). The excavators say the base agrees with the documents, with rooms 4.48 m wide and eaves columns 3.68 m (S139; E1643). Malone puts it about a quarter mile east of 日天琳宇 (S02 p.89; E1639).

A short mhymy record without sheet data (S310 rec. 2579) places the 田-shaped hall north of the 后湖, south-west of 舍卫城 Shewei Cheng, built by 1727. The 初编 has one page, p.266 (E1642). No 丈尺 was found in any Qing source read here; the documents the excavators compared with were not seen.
YM20.interior_en: Plaques: 澹泊宁静 (Qianlong's hand) on the north tower; south gate 亦复佳, west gate 得山水趣, behind the north gallery 麦雨稻风, and 曙光楼, all Qianlong's; 多稼轩, 观稼轩, 怡情悦目, 稻香亭, 溪山不尽, 兰溪隐玉 in Yongzheng's hand (S05 j81:29b; E1633). Couplets of 多稼轩 (Qianlong): "風裊爐烟移晝漏 月臨書幌正宵衣" and "厥惟艱哉載芟載柞籌穡事 亦既勤止曰暘曰雨驗農時" (S05 j81:29b-30a). A copy of Lou Shu's 耕织图 Gengzhi Tu by Cheng Qi was kept in this group (S361 v2 p.185; E1670). Pot plum in 静香屋 ("盆梅几朵才舒蕊", E1654).
YM20.setting_en: Rice paddies as far as the eye could see ("稻田彌望"), with water all round ("河水周環") (S05 j81:29a; E1633). Shade trees, flowers and reeds (E1618). In the west court: a rock stream, a bamboo-roofed pavilion, a pond of Rehe carp fed by a sluice (S05 j81:30b-33b; E1620); a real waterfall through an artificial rockery at 水精域 (E1653); a small rockery climbed to 寸碧亭 (E1658); 互妙楼 half up a hill (E1660); 招鹤磴, a stone stair named for calling cranes (E1656, E1657). The dig found pebble aprons and paddy soil of the imperial rice field (S137; E1644).
YM20.survives_en: Three seasons from November 2020 by the park, the 北京市文物研究所 and Peking University exposed the whole base of the 田字房: 33 rooms each about 4.48 m square, gallery 1.28 m, the base standing about 0.55 m, with column bases, floor bricks, drains, steps and pebble aprons, all heavily burnt; paddy of the imperial rice fields was found too (S139; S137; S138). The scene measures about 140 m N-S by 160 m E-W, 26,000 m2, with 1,350 m2 of buildings (S139).
YM20.what_zh: 澹泊宁静位于日天琳宇以东稍南，“稻田彌望河水周環”，中有田字形殿，四面设门，东、北两面有楼，北楼正宇即名澹泊宁静（S05 j81:29a；E1633），至迟建于雍正五年（1727）（E1640；S310）。殿西门外另有院墙，内有南向七间的多稼轩和一组以农事为题的建筑，乾隆二十四年（1759）乾隆帝作十景诗，次年小修（E1620；E1647）；《圆明园五朝御制诗文集注》将这组建筑归入映水兰香（E1670）。乾隆帝曾在稻香亭观看收割（E1651）。1860年10月18日至19日英军焚园时被毁（E0485）。2020年至2022年考古发掘揭露了田字房的全部基址，基址、院落和道路均有严重火烧痕迹，发掘者认为与1860年大火有关（S137；S139；E1644）。
YM20.survives_zh: 自2020年11月起，圆明园管理处、北京市文物研究所与北京大学连续三期发掘，揭露田字房全部基址：共33间，每间约4.48米见方，廊宽1.28米，台基残高约0.55米，存柱础、地面砖、排水沟、台阶和卵石散水，均有严重火烧痕迹；还发现了御稻田的水田遗迹（S139；S137；S138）。整个景区南北约140米、东西约160米，占地约2.6万平方米，建筑面积约1350平方米（S139）。
YM20.summary_en: The rice-field scene: a hall on the plan of the character 田 among paddies, standing by 1727, with a farm-themed court to the west; its burnt base was dug in 2020-2022 (E1633; E1640; E1644).
YM20.scene_zh: 《圆明园四十景图》第二十幅（P0020）。乾隆帝诗序说：“仿田字為房密室周遮塵氛不到”，屋外槐荫花蔓、流水涟漪、芦苇苍苍。景名出自诸葛亮“澹泊以明志，宁静以致远”，诗中称之为“武侯妙語”（S40；E1618）。
YM20.summary_zh: 澹泊宁静是稻田中的田字形殿堂，至迟建于1727年，其焚毁后的基址已于2020年至2022年发掘（E1633；E1640；E1644）。

YM13.what_en: 万方安和 Wanfang Anhe, "Peace and Harmony Everywhere", stood north-west of 杏花春馆 Xinghua Chunguan: a building raised in the lake on the plan of the sign 卍 (S05 j81:9a; E1447). It was built by 1727 (S361 v2 p.117; E1451; S310 rec. 7980). Each arm of the 卍 held named rooms; the main room, sunny and facing south, was at the south-east (S05 j81:10a-12a; E1442). Qianlong says his father liked to live here, warm in winter and cool in summer (S40; E1441). Malone: on a brick and stone foundation, entirely surrounded by water, with a much smaller cross-plan building at the south end of the lake (S02 p.81; E1450). 平安院 Ping'an Yuan lay north-east across a bridge, and a large double-eaved cross-shaped pavilion stood on the south shore (S361; E1451). It was lost when British troops burned the gardens on 18-19 October 1860 (E0485).
YM13.scene_en: Leaf 13 of the 1744 album (P0013). Qianlong's preface: "水心架搆形作卍字畧彴相通" (built in the heart of the water in the form of 卍, joined to the shore by small plank bridges). From it one sees rare flowers on the far shore like brocade; on clear autumn nights under the moon "此百尺地寜非佛胸涌出寳光耶", these hundred feet seem the radiance from the Buddha's breast. His note says Yongzheng liked to live here, warm in winter, cool in summer (S40, printed in S05 j81:9b-10a; E1441).
YM13.later_en:
In 1764 Qianlong wrote nine poems on the four-character plaques, all in Yongzheng's hand, and his preface says the gallery runs round every side and each turn gives a different view (S05 j81:10a-12a; E1442). The 日下旧闻考 note reads the plaques arm by arm (S05 j81:9a-9b; E1447), which places each room on its arm: south main room 万方安和; east-west inner rooms 对溪山, 佳气迎人; centre 四方宁静; west 观妙音, 枕流漱石, 洞天深处; east 安然, 一炉香, 碧溪一带, 山水清音; north 涤尘心, 神洲三岛, 高山流水, all in Yongzheng's hand; on the west wing of the south arm 凝神, 静寄, and on the east 澄观, in Qianlong's hand. 端木泓 Duanmu Hong, in an article seen only as an abstract, reads the whole as a Buddhist cosmic diagram, with the 十字亭 and the long hall of 山高水长 as answering strokes (S357; E1453): an interpretation, not evidence.

The one plan found is 样053-1-2, 万方安和地盘全样 (NLC, 1650x744 mm, ink, light colour, red and yellow slips, paste-overs, presentation sheet, 乾嘉时期; E1456; S310 rec. 7980): earlier than 1860 by decades. The Palace Museum card model (烫样) of 万方安和殿, shown in Hong Kong in 2024, is reported to be of the Tongzhi repair (S326, search extract; S261; S920): a design of 1873-74, not the hall of 1860. The mhymy record calls the building 万字房 and says it stood by 雍正五年 (1727) (S310 rec. 7980).
YM13.interior_en: Centre couplet (Qianlong): "四海昇平承帝眷 萬幾兢業亮天工" (S05 j81:9b; E1447). The poems give room features: the centre room square with galleries on all four sides ("四面尽通廊，中间正且方", E1462); the north room 神洲三岛 has a loft inside ("室中亦有楼", E1466); 高山流水 has a spring led in and rocks piled ("疏泉还叠石", E1467); 碧溪一带 looks east down a long stream with mist entering the low windows (E1463). 佳气迎人 is reached turning west then north to the middle ("向西旋转北，步近室之中", E1460).
YM13.setting_en:
Built in open water, joined to the shores by plank bridges (E1441); a brick and stone base (S02 p.81; E1450). Reed islets and willow dykes in the poems ("秋月芦花渚，春风柳线隄", E1463). Flowers on the far bank (E1441). A cross-shaped pavilion on the south shore (E1450, E1451).

P0013 shows the swastika building in the lake on high white stone bases with ochre inset panels and steps to the water, grey 歇山 roofs on each wing, red-brown columns, a white arched bridge at its east end and timber bridges with red railings elsewhere; a cross-plan pavilion with a gilt finial stands on the south-west shore. The 卍 plan is only partly legible from this angle; the woodcut P0096 shows how the wings meet. Autumn trees. (S08 P0013, crop ym13_c1; S76 P0096)
YM13.survives_en: The cross-shaped 卍 platform stands in its pond, restored: its arms are paved terraces with stone edges at one level, with channels between them (P0381). A dig of 2003 found the original stone trough of the 响水 'sounding water' cascade on the west shore, where a Yangshi Lei drawing writes 响水; the cascade was repaired and set running again, smaller than the drawing shows (S944).
YM13.what_zh: 万方安和位于杏花春馆西北，建于湖中，平面呈“卍”字形（S05 j81:9a；E1447），至迟建于雍正五年（1727）（E1451；S310）。卍字各臂皆有题名的房间，向阳正室在东南（E1442）。乾隆帝说此处“冬燠夏爽”，是其父雍正帝喜居之所（E1441）。马龙（Malone）记其建于砖石基座上，四面环水，湖南端另有一座较小的十字形建筑（E1450）。东北有桥通平安院，南岸有重檐十字亭（E1451）。1860年10月18日至19日英军焚园时被毁（E0485）。
YM13.survives_zh: 卍字形台基仍立于水中，经过修整：各臂为同一高度、石砌边缘的铺装平台，臂间有水道（P0381）。2003年发掘在西岸发现原有的石砌“响水”水槽，样式雷图上此处注有“响水”；此后水景修复重新放水，规模小于图样所示（S944）。
YM13.summary_en: A building raised in the lake on the plan of the sign 卍, standing by 1727, with named rooms on every arm; Yongzheng liked to live here, warm in winter and cool in summer (E1447; E1451; E1441).
YM13.scene_zh: 《圆明园四十景图》第十三幅（P0013）。乾隆帝诗序说：“水心架搆形作卍字畧彴相通”，遥望对岸奇花如锦绣；秋夜月下，“此百尺地寜非佛胸涌出寳光耶”。注中说雍正帝喜居于此，冬暖夏凉（S40；E1441）。
YM13.summary_zh: 万方安和是建于湖中的卍字形建筑，至迟建于1727年，为雍正帝喜居之所（E1447；E1451；E1441）。

YM09.en: The Springtime Lodge of Apricot Blossoms
YM09.what_en: 杏花春馆 Xinghua Chunguan, "Spring Lodge of Apricot Blossom", on the island south-west of 上下天光, reached across a bridge (S05 j81:1a; E1296). First a vegetable plot with a plaque of 1727; 春雨轩 was added in 1755 (S361 v2 p.25; E1303; S360 p.147, Qianlong's poem on its completion "别殿落成歌", E1287). The island holds the highest hill of the main garden but for the rock hill in the north-west, crowned by the small gate 屏岩, with the hexagonal pavilion 绿云酣 half way up (S02 p.80; E1301; S41; E1308). The main earth-god shrine of the garden stood south-west of it, facing east (S47; E1302). The editors say 春雨轩 and others outlived 1860 and were lost around 1900 (E1303); offerings were still made at the shrine in 1861 (S47 p.126; E1315). 屏岩 and 绿云酣 were excavated in 2020 (S41; E1308).
YM09.scene_en: Leaf 9 of the 1744 album. Qianlong's preface: "矮屋疎籬東西參錯環植文杏春深花發爛然如霞" (low cottages and sparse fences scattered east and west, ringed with apricot trees that in late spring blaze like rosy cloud). A small plot of mixed vegetables in front gives the look of a farm village; the poem ends on spring rain and the plough (S40, printed in S05 j81:1b-2a; E1285).
YM09.later_en:
By the 1780s the group was 杏花春馆 with 春雨轩 to the north-west, 杏花村 west of the 轩, 涧壑余清 south of the village, 镜水斋 behind the 轩 to the east, 抑斋 a north-west room, and 翠微堂 further west (S05 j81:1a; E1296). The editors add 得树亭, 吟籁亭, the gate 渊镜/屏岩 and 绿云酣 (E1303). Malone notes that the album shows rustic buildings, a well and vegetable plots, while the later plan S01 shows a pond instead of the plots and more buildings instead of the well (S02 p.80 n.32; E1301): the scene was rebuilt between 1744 and the plan's state. The shrine was named 春雨轩土地庙 in an archive file of 1858, when Xianfeng gave its two deities titles, tablets and a stele (S47; E1302).

Plan 样028-1 (NLC, ink, working sheet, 1831-1840; E1305). The record: first a vegetable plot 菜圃 under Kangxi; plaques 杏花春馆 and 杏花村 hung 1727; the 1744 leaf shows low huts, fences and apricots; in 1755 the front was rebuilt with the 春雨轩 hall, the 涧壑余清 gate and the 得树 pavilion; 1770 a rock peak behind 春雨轩; at the end of Qianlong 19 buildings of 71 bays were repainted, two of them of 楠木 (S310 rec. 8065). So the 1744 leaf is not the 1860 state here.
YM09.interior_en: Plaque 杏花春馆 in Yongzheng's hand; Qianlong's 1744 poem cut on a rock beside the lodge ("館旁峰石上刋御製杏花春館詩"); inside 春雨轩 the plaque 蕙气清阴, and on its rear porch the couplet "生機對物觀其妙 義府因心獲所寜"; plaques of 镜水斋, 抑斋, 翠微堂 in Qianlong's hand (S05 j81:1a; E1296). Tablets and a stele added to the earth shrine in 1858 (E1302).
YM09.setting_en: Apricot trees (文杏) all round the cottages, a vegetable plot and a well in 1744 (E1285, E1301); later a pond in place of the plots (E1301). A hill with a small city gate at the top and a hexagonal pavilion on its slope (E1308). On the album the gable walls of the earth shrine are painted red, against grey or white on other buildings (S47 pp.121-123; E0499).

YM14.what_en: 武陵春色 Wuling Chunse, "Spring Colours of Wuling", the peach-blossom valley reached over a bridge behind 万方安和, east and a little north, south of a rock tunnel (S05 j81:12b; E1492). Finished 1726 after Tao Yuanming's Peach Blossom Spring; first named 桃花坞 as a whole; Qianlong lived and read here as a prince from 1726 and called his study 乐善堂 before moving to 长春仙馆 (S05 j81:13a; E1492; S361 v2 p.132; E1500). The visitor came by boat up the stream through the cave 壶中天 to a pool with its halls (E1500; S02 p.81; E1499). Under Jiaqing 恒春堂 was added for theatre, with the two-storey stage 壶中仙籁 (S43 1.8; E1501; E1513, E1514). Burned in October 1860.
YM14.scene_en: Leaf 14 of the 1744 album. Qianlong's preface: "循溪流而北複谷環抱山桃萬株" (following the stream north, valleys fold round, with ten thousand mountain peach trees). Petals fall and float on the water; at dawn and dusk the trees blaze like snow and flushed cloud. The quatrain: "複岫迴環一水通", ring upon ring of hills with one stream through them (S40, printed in S05 j81:14b-15a; E1472).
YM14.later_en:
日下旧闻考 lists, from the cave: 武陵春色 with 壶中日月长 north of the pool, 天然佳妙 to the east and 洞天日月多佳景 on the south porch; 全璧堂 to the west with the pavilion 小隐栖迟 south-east; behind, through a gap in the hills, 清秀亭 east and 清会亭 west; 桃花坞 north, 清水濯缨 its west room, 桃源深处 further west; 绾春轩 east of the 坞 and 品诗堂 north-east of the 轩 (S05 j81:12b-13a; E1492). The editors add the five-bay 天君泰然 and, under Jiaqing, 恒春堂 (S361; E1500). Jiaqing wrote on 恒春堂 in 1812 and 1813 (E1513, E1514); plays are on record at its stage in 1819 and 1839 (S43; E1501).

Only a short record without catalogue data (S310 rec. 2812; E1504): built before 1720 as 桃花坞, a rock tunnel in the south-east entered by boat, halls 壶中日月长 (five-bay open hall north of the pool), 天然佳妙, 洞天日月多佳景, 桃源深处, 绾春轩, 品诗堂. No drawing number seen; the 初编 has pp.267-286 on it (E1503).
YM14.interior_en: Plaques: inside the cave 壶中天; 壶中日月长, 天然佳妙, 洞天日月多佳景, 小隐栖迟, 清秀, 清会亭, 桃花坞, 清水濯缨, 桃源深处 in Yongzheng's hand; 全璧堂, 绾春轩, 品诗堂 in Qianlong's (S05 j81:13a-13b; E1492). The stage carried 天上云璈 and 壶中仙籁 (S43; E1501). 品诗堂 is where Qianlong had studied and written as a young man (E1511, E1512).
YM14.setting_en: A closed valley of hills round a stream, ten thousand peach trees on the slopes (E1472). A canal passes through a cave under the hill on the east side and out on the other (S02 p.81; E1499). Willows at 绾春轩 ("百尺垂丝绿影铺", E1509; "柳色微黄", E1510). Birdsong and dogs barking beyond the stream in the poem on 桃源深处 (E1508).

YM31.what_en: 平湖秋月 Pinghu Qiuyue, "Autumn Moon on the Calm Lake", in the north-west corner of 福海 (S05 j82:15b; E1912): a three-bay main hall set against a hill and facing the lake, with plank bridges on either side (S40; E1896). Around it 流水音 to the west, 花屿兰皋 by the river out of a gap in the hills to the north-east, 两峰插云 across a bridge to the south-east, 山水乐 further south-east, and 君子轩 and 藏密楼 to the north (S05 j82:15b; E1912). In 1810 Jiaqing rebuilt part of it and named it 镜远洲, writing on it every year to 1820 (S360; E1917). Burned in October 1860.
YM31.scene_en: Leaf 31 of the 1744 album, a 浣溪纱 lyric. Preface: "倚山面湖竹樹䝉密左右支板橋以通步屐" (against the hill, facing the lake, dense with bamboo and trees, plank bridges on left and right for walkers). The lake runs to tens of qing and on deep autumn nights moonlight and water join the sky; the view equals Su Shi's causeway on 西湖. The lyric opens "不辨天光與水光" (S40, printed in S05 j82:15b-16a; E1896).
YM31.later_en: Qianlong wrote on 君子轩, 藏密楼 and 夏隐亭 from 1759 to 1795 (S360; E1897-E1905, E1914-E1916); 藏密楼 is climbed by red stairs and has green windows ("丹梯拾级因髙迥，绿牖凭虚纳远通", S361 v2 p.368; E1923). Jiaqing's 镜远洲 of 1810 (E1917); Daoguang wrote on 平湖秋月 in 1823 and 1824, Xianfeng in 1857 (E1909-E1911). The Yangshi Lei sheets are in S13 (E1918). Note: S361 files the poems on 流水音 and 藏密楼 under 澡身浴德, not under this scene (E1920, E1923, E1924).
YM31.interior_en: Plaque 平湖秋月 in Yongzheng's hand; 流水音, 花屿兰皋 and the others in Qianlong's (S05 j82:15b; E1912). No inventory seen.
YM31.setting_en: Dense bamboo and trees, plank bridges on either side, the hill behind (E1896); smartweed and lotus ("蓼煙荷露", E1896). At 流水音 water drips from piled rocks into a cave ("叠石崚嶒泉细注，泠然岩底出清音", Jiaqing 1798; E1920). A river and a hill gap at 花屿兰皋; a bridge to 两峰插云 (E1912).
YM31.gaps_en: No sheet found on mhymy; the 初编 has one page, p.441 (E1918). 样043-1 shows its layout like the base drawing of 样1704, unlike 样1370 and 样1196 (S310 rec. 9509).

YM39.what_en: 曲院风荷 Quyuan Fenghe, "Lotus in the Breeze at the Brewery Yard", east of 碧桐书院 and south-east of 坐石临流: a five-bay hall facing south, with the Buddhist tower 洛迦胜境 to its west (S05 j82:26b; E2077). South of it a nine-opening bridge crossed the lotus pool east-west between two archways, 金鳌 west and 玉蝀 east; 四围佳丽 beyond the river south-west of 金鳌; the pavilion 饮练长虹 east of 玉蝀; then over a bridge north-east the walled mock town gate 宁和镇 and, south-east of it, 东楼门 (S05 j82:27a-27b; E2078). 宁和镇 was renamed 春和镇 early in Daoguang's reign (S361 v3 p.112; E2081), which matches the plan's 春和镇. Burned in October 1860; in 1871 the 金鳌 and 玉蝀 archways still stood (S203; E0433).
YM39.scene_en: Leaf 39 of the 1744 album. Preface: "西湖麴院為宋時酒務地荷花最多" (the brewery yard on West Lake, a Song state brewery, had the most lotus). Here red lotus covers the water and the long bridge's reflection sways, so the place takes that name. The quatrain sets a pair of ducks asleep under the flowers (S40, printed in S05 j82:26b-27a; E2073).
YM39.later_en:
日下旧闻考 gives the bridge and archways (E2078). Malone: a great curved bridge on nine arches over a pretty lotus pond, "leading nowhere in particular" (S02 pp.94-96; E2080). Name 宁和镇 to 春和镇 under Daoguang (E2081; E2393).

Record 2455 (no catalogue data; E2083): a long narrow lotus pool crossed by a nine-arch stone bridge, embankments round it and a stream beyond; the buildings (曲院风荷, 洛伽胜境) on a small island north of the pool across a stream, joined by winding galleries. The 初编 has one page, p.228 (E2082).
YM39.interior_en: Plaques 曲院风荷 and 洛迦胜境 in Qianlong's hand; 饮练长虹 and 宁和镇 also (S05 j82:26b-27b; E2077, E2078). 洛迦胜境 is a Buddhist tower, so it held images; no inventory seen.
YM39.setting_en:
A lotus pool with red lotus ("紅衣印波", E2073) crossed by the nine-opening bridge with an archway at each end (E2078, E2080). Ducks (E2073).

P0039 draws the nine-arch bridge 九孔桥 frontally: nine round arches rising to the centre, white arch rings and balustrade, yellow-brown stone spandrels, a 牌坊 with red props at the west end and a double-eaved octagonal pavilion and second 牌坊 at the east end; behind it a walled street of small houses with a gate tower (宁和镇, my tie). The woodcut P0088 shows lotus over the lake. (S08 P0039, crop ym39_c1; S76 P0088)

YM38.en: The Stone Resting in the Running Water
YM38.what_en: 坐石临流 Zuoshi Linliu, "Sitting on Rocks by the Stream", south-east of 水木明瑟 and east of 澹泊宁静: a three-bay hall facing west, ringed by stream (S05 j82:25b; E2064). The album shows a pavilion over a rocky gully where the stream divides, for the cup-floating game, with 同乐园 to the east (S40; E2056). The scene name covered a district: the shop street with its theatre, the bridge and the walled 舍卫城 (S02 p.94; E2067; S361 v3 p.88; E2068). A Republic-period note says the old 兰亭 of the garden had a stone with a picture and an imperial poem and eight pillars carved with famous copies; after the ruin the stone went to the Central Park and the pillars were found at 颐和园 (S215; E2070); the pillars survive at 中山公园, Beijing (T040; S408; S409). Burned in October 1860.
YM38.scene_en: Leaf 38 of the 1744 album. Preface: "仄澗中潨泉奔滙竒石峭列" (in a narrow gully the springs race together, past sharp-set rocks). The divided stream sings and can float wine cups; a pavilion stands at the best spot, 同乐园 to the east. The quatrain ends "便是當時晉永和", the Lanting gathering of 353 (S40, printed in S05 j82:26a; E2056).
YM38.later_en: 日下旧闻考 says only three bays facing west and ringed by stream, with Qianlong's plaque (S05 j82:25b; E2064); it names no 兰亭 or eight pillars here (checked on Kanripo KR2k0036_082, j82:25b-26b). The eight-pillar 兰亭 comes from later texts: a Republic-period note on the old 蘭亭 with its stone and eight pillars carved with famous copies (S215; E2070), the scene card (S340; E2069), and the twin row T040: the pillars stand today in a pavilion at 中山公园, reached there in two stages, before 1917 and after 1941 (S408; S409). Search extracts date the cutting of the 兰亭八柱帖 to 1779 (乾隆四十四年); not seen on a page I fetched. If so, the pillar pavilion postdates the album and most of 日下旧闻考, and the state of 1860 is the 1779 one. Jiaqing's poem of 1796 describes it: "仿成亭子俯平坡。山屏镂刻图全展，石柱周环帖遍罗", a pavilion copied (from the Lanting) above the slope, a stone screen carved with the whole picture, stone pillars all round covered with the copies (S361 v3 p.97; E2062). In 1806 he wrote on the thatched 抱朴草堂 of the same district (E2063), which the editors call a six-bay reverse-facing hall (E2068).
YM38.interior_en: The Lanting pavilion: a stone screen carved with the picture (of the Lanting gathering) and stone pillars all round carrying the copies of the Lanting calligraphy (Jiaqing 1796: "山屏镂刻图全展，石柱周环帖遍罗"; S361 v3 p.97; E2062); a Republic note adds an imperial poem on the stone (S215; E2070). The eight pillars survive at 中山公园 (T040; S408; S409). In the thatched 抱朴草堂: paper windows and a rattan couch ("纸窗藤榻欣清雅", Jiaqing 1806; E2063). Plaque 坐石临流 in Qianlong's hand (S05 j82:25b; E2064).
YM38.setting_en: White rocks, clear spring, green creeper, a winding stream with golden lotus ("白石清泉帶碧蘿曲流貼貼泛金荷") (S40; E2056); sharp rocks forming islets and coves (E2056).
YM38.gaps_en: No own sheet on mhymy. 样043-1 shows the eight-sided pavilion at 坐石临流, rebuilt in mid-Qianlong as 八方重檐亭 with a hexagonal thatched pavilion, a square bamboo-style pavilion and a two-bay thatched house (archive text quoted on S310 rec. 9509).
YM38.role_en: The Granite Road South of She Wei Ch'eng

YM33.en: The House Which Meets the Beauty of the Hills
YM33.what_en: 接秀山房 Jiexiu Shanfang, "Mountain Lodge that Greets Beauty", at the east corner of 福海: a three-bay main hall facing west across the lake, 琴趣轩 behind to the east, the square tower 寻云 to the north, 澄练楼 to the south-east with 怡然书屋 behind it, the Buddhist room 安隐幢 east of 寻云楼, and 揽翠亭 to the south (S05 j82:17b-18a; E1954). Begun 1731 (S361 v3 p.1; E1957). About 1817 Jiaqing built 观澜堂, five bays in three rolls, the largest hall on 福海 (S360 p.272; E1956; S361; E1957). A Yangshi Lei plan of 观澜堂 is dated 1855 (S310 样042-11-2号; E1958). The editors say 观澜堂 outlived 1860, that Cixi came in 1898, and that it was lost around 1900 (E1957).
YM33.scene_en: Leaf 33 of the 1744 album. Preface: "平岡縈迴碧沚停蓄虛館閒閒境獨夷曠" (low ridges wind round, a green pool lies still, an empty lodge stands quiet, the place alone open and wide). Across the water peaks show their beauty, blue in the morning haze, purple at dusk. The poem: "户接西山秀", the door greets the beauty of the Western Hills (S40, printed in S05 j82:18a-18b; E1945).
YM33.later_en: Plaques of 1744 (接秀山房, 揽翠亭) are Yongzheng's, those of 琴趣轩 and 寻云 Qianlong's (S05 j82:17b; E1954). Qianlong came by boat to 澄练楼 ("湖上乘舟至，登楼更望湖", 1763; E1962). Jiaqing's 观澜堂 of about 1817 (E1956, E1957); Jiaqing and Xianfeng poems on it in 1819 and 1857 (E1966, E1953). The sources disagree on what 观澜堂 replaced: S360 says 观鱼跃 was pulled down for a south-facing hall (E1956), S361 that the main hall was replaced (E1957). Modern plans also disagree which base along the east shore is which; S338 reads them north to south ending with 云锦墅 and 观澜堂 (E2019).
YM33.interior_en: Plaques as above (E1954). The poems on 琴趣轩 say no zither hangs on the wall: the music is the dripping spring ("无弦亦不壁间悬", E1961; "暗泉滴处声同调", E1960). 怡然书屋 had book shelves ("架是琳琅笥", E1964).
YM33.setting_en: Low ridges and a still green pool, the Western Hills seen across 福海 (E1945); pines and bamboo ("松竹古之朋", E1945). A hidden spring at 琴趣轩 (E1960). 观澜堂 looked north to the hills and west to the ranges ("北峙群峰印云素，西排列岫染霞丹", 1819; E1966).

YM04.what_en: 镂月开云 Louyue Kaiyun, first called 牡丹台 Mudan Tai, the Peony Terrace, stood behind 富春楼 Fuchun Lou on the east side of the Back Lake; its main hall is 纪恩堂 Ji'en Tang, with 御兰芬 Yulanfen to the north (S05 j80:26a). The old name was replaced in 1744 and the plaque 纪恩堂 was hung in 1766 (乾隆三十一年), with an essay recalling that here Yongzheng, then a prince, presented the young Hongli to the Kangxi Emperor at a peony viewing, after which Kangxi took him into the palace (S05 j80:26b-28b). Burned in October 1860 with the rest of the garden by British troops on Elgin's order (S02 pp.187-188).
YM04.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "殿以香楠為材覆二色瓦煥若金碧前植牡丹數百本後列古松青青" (S05 j80:30a). The hall was built of fragrant nanmu and roofed with tiles of two colours, shining like gold and jade; several hundred peonies grew in front and old pines behind. A note in the poem says the peonies peak in the fourth month, when the capital is usually praying for rain, so in seven years of residence he had feasted at the blossom only once (S05 j80:30a-b; same theme in the 1746 poem E1196, S360).
YM04.later_en: S05 (1774+) names only 纪恩堂 and 御兰芬; the 1766 and 1767 poems add 养素书屋 Yangsu Shuwu beside 御兰芬, and a 1767 poem says the orchid hall 御兰芬 stood directly behind the peony terrace ("偶臨蘭蕙畹前即牡丹臺", E1198-E1200, S360). On the base plan S01 the main hall carries a label read only as "?云楼", not 纪恩堂, and the pavilion 来青亭 Laiqing Ting (YM04-N01) appears, which S05 does not name: so the plan state differs from the 1774 text at least in naming. No dated Jiaqing-Xianfeng rebuild was found in this pass.
YM04.setting_en: Peonies in hundreds in front of the hall, old pines behind, mixed flowering plants all round (S05 j80:30a); orchids at 御兰芬 beside white rocks, a clear spring, pine and bamboo (E1197, S360 1766 poem: "白石清泉側蒼松翠竹倫"). Roof of two-colour glazed tiles is the one stated colour scheme (S05 j80:30a); which two colours is not said.
YM04.survives_en: No dig report for 镂月开云 was found in this pass; only the plan footprints (S01) and the album leaf P0004 stand for it.
YM04.gaps_en: The leaf P0004 shows the front hall with a green-glazed roof edged in dark blue, which is probably the 二色瓦 'two-colour tiles' of the preface (my reading of the painting, C); the bays of 纪恩堂 (plan 9 cells by 2, which may include galleries); whether the plan label "?云楼" is a misreading of 镂月开云 or a later name.

YM05.what_en: 天然图画 Tianran Tuhua, on the east bank of the Back Lake north of 镂月开云: the tower 天然图画楼, with 朗吟阁 Langyin Ge to the north, 竹薖楼 Zhuke Lou further north, 五福堂 Wufu Tang of five bays to the east, a five-bay hall 竹深荷净 Zhushen Hejing behind it to the north, 静知春事佳 Jingzhi Chunshi Jia to the south-east, and across the stream 苏堤春晓 Sudi Chunxiao (S05 j80:31b). Most plaques are by Yongzheng; that of 五福堂 by Kangxi, so the core predates 1723 (S05 j80:32a). The garden was burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188), but 文昌阁 Wenchang Ge (YM05-08, tie 'likely') stood among the 17 buildings 刘敦桢 listed as left after the fire in 1933 (E0451, S337).
YM05.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "庭前修篁萬竿與雙桐相暎風枝露梢緑滿襟䄂西為髙樓折而南翼以重榭" (S05 j80:32b). Ten thousand bamboos and two paulownias in the court; a tall tower on the west, turning south into two-storey pavilions, with distant views beyond what a painter could do. The poem warns against carved walls and lofty halls even while praising them.
YM05.later_en: 五福堂 was renamed 五福五代堂 in 甲辰 1784, when Qianlong, then past seventy, saw his great-great-grandson: 'in 甲辰 I saw my 元孙 and added two characters, 五福五代堂' (E1225, S360, 1790 poem note). The plaque 五福堂 was Kangxi's, given to Yongzheng and hung first in his princely residence, now 雍和宫 (E1226). S01 writes 五福五代堂 (YM05-04): so the plan is post-1784. 竹深荷净 (YM05-05) carries a label read "?静斋" on an 11-cell row, another post-S05 change.
YM05.setting_en: Bamboo grove and twin paulownias in the court, the Back Lake to the west, a stream to the east crossed to 苏堤春晓, named after the Su causeway of West Lake (S05 j80:31b-32b). 竹薖楼 had an eave plaque 桃花春一溪 by Yongzheng, i.e. peach trees along a stream (S05 j80:32a).
YM05.gaps_en: No dig found; storeys of 天然图画楼 and 朗吟阁 not stated in S05 (楼 and 阁 imply two). The renaming to 五福五代堂 needs a date (S360 likely has it).

YM06.en: Library of the Green Wu T'ung Trees
YM06.what_en: 碧桐书院 Bitong Shuyuan, "Library of the Green Paulownias", lay north of 五福堂 across the stream, enclosed by hills: a front hall of three bays, a main hall of five, and a rear hall 后照殿 of five, with 云岑亭 Yuncen Ting on rocks to the west (S05 j80:34b). The plaque is by Yongzheng, so it existed before 1735 (S05 j80:35a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM06.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "前接平橋環以帶水庭左右修梧數本緑隂張蓋" (S05 j80:35a): a flat bridge in front, a belt of water round it, tall paulownias left and right of the court spreading shade; the emperor liked the sound of rain on their leaves.
