YM06.interior_en: Malone was told by a palace painter that the Tongzhi Emperor was born in 慎德堂 on the 九洲清晏 island; another tradition, 'Yuan's memorandum', says in 'Pi T'ao Shu Yuan', which Malone takes to mean 碧桐书院 (S02 p.79 n.). He also says four paulownias (wu t'ung) stood in its courts (S02 p.79).
YM06.setting_en: A closed court of three halls on one axis (3, 5, 5 bays), water round it and a flat bridge at the front, hills round the north, paulownias in the court, a rock with a pavilion on the west (S05 j80:34b-35a).
YM06.gaps_en: Only 14 evidence rows; no dig; S360 records not read in this pass.

YM07.what_en: 慈云普护 Ciyun Puhu, the shrine island on the north shore of the Back Lake, west of 碧桐书院: a front hall of three bays facing the lake, 欢喜佛场 Huanxi Fochang; north of it a three-bay storeyed building with the plaque 慈云普护, Guanyin above and Guandi below; to the east 龙王殿, the shrine of the Dragon King of the garden, 昭福龙王 (S05 j80:35b-36a). Plaques by Yongzheng (S05 j80:36a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM07.scene_en: Lyric of 1744 (to 菩薩蠻): "有樓三層刻漏鐘表在焉殿供觀音大士其傍為道士廬" (S05 j80:36b). A path runs between two lakes under wisteria; there is a three-storey tower holding a water clock and clocks, a hall for Guanyin and beside it a Daoist's lodge, like the stone bridge of Tiantai.
YM07.setting_en: On a strip between two waters (一徑界重湖間), with wisteria on trellises and tree-peonies (鼠姑) (S05 j80:36b). The clock tower is the scene's landmark on the album leaf; S01 marks a 钟亭 (YM07-N01).
YM07.gaps_en: The three-storey tower of the lyric (樓三層刻漏鐘表, S05 j80:36b) is on the leaf P0007 a separate hexagonal red tower with three roofs, standing west of the two-storey 慈云普护 hall: it is the 钟亭 of S01 (YM07-N01), not the three-bay hall. Its size and the clockwork are not described. No dig.

YM08.what_en: 上下天光 Shangxia Tianguang, west of 慈云普护 on the north shore of the Back Lake: a lakeside tower of three bays on each floor, a hexagonal pavilion on each side, and 平安院 Ping'an Yuan behind (S05 j80:37a). Plaque and couplet by Qianlong; the right pavilion 饮和 Yinhe and 平安院 by Yongzheng, the left pavilion 奇赏 Qishang by Qianlong (S05 j80:37b). The park's survey gives 10,500 m2 of site and 1,600 m2 of buildings, and says that early Yongzheng had only the two-storey tower and a timber bridge pavilion, while under Daoguang the upper floor was closed in and a square pavilion, a service court and an open hall were added (E1280, S152). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM08.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "垂虹駕湖蜿蜒百尺修欄夾翼中為廣亭" (S05 j80:38a). A rainbow-like bridge winds a hundred 尺 across the lake, long rails on both sides and a broad pavilion in the middle; looking down from the tower, water and sky are one colour, as at Dongting.
YM08.later_en: Changes between the 1744 leaf and 1860, per the survey report: under Daoguang the open upper floor was enclosed and a square pavilion, a service court and an open hall were added (E1280, S152). The 1860 model must therefore show the enclosed upper storey, not the open gallery of the album.
YM08.gaps_en: Bridge length is only the poetic 百尺 (about 32 m); the Daoguang-era layout of the added square pavilion is not located.
YM08.role_en: The Island of the Zig-zag Bridges

YM10.what_en: 坦坦荡荡 Tantan Dangdang, the fish-pond scene on the west shore of the Back Lake, earlier called 鱼池 'the fish pond' (S05 j81:2b; the old name only in a search extract). S05: a three-bay 坦坦荡荡 hall, 素心堂 Suxin Tang as the front hall, 光风霁月 Guangfeng Jiyue as the rear hall, 知鱼亭 Zhiyu Ting to the north-east, 萃景斋 Cuijing Zhai further north-east and 双佳斋 Shuangjia Zhai to the north-west (S05 j81:2b). The editors of S361 read the layout as a five-bay gate hall 素心堂 with an annex, 半亩园 Banmu Yuan east, 澹怀堂 west, and the five-bay 光风霁月 standing in the middle of the pool (E1333). Malone too places 光风霁月 in mid-tank, bridged on all four sides (E1332, S02). Daoguang still dined with the dowager at 半亩园 in 1839 (E1328, S360). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM10.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "鑿池為魚樂國池周舍下錦鱗數千頭" (S05 j81:3a). A pool was dug as a 'kingdom of happy fish' with thousands of brocade-scaled fish around and under the buildings; the poem turns Zhuangzi's 'joy of fish' into the ruler's concern for his people (我蒿目乎斯民). The poem was also cut on a rock at 萃景斋 (S05 j81:3a).
YM10.later_en: S05 lists six names; S360 adds 碧澜亭 Bilan Ting (poems 1764-1795, E1331) and 半亩园 (in use 1839, E1328), and the plan S01 labels the main hall '坦:荡:' on a 15-cell row (YM10-01): the scene grew east and west after 1744. 素心堂 has poems to 1819 (E1329).
YM10.survives_en: Excavated from spring 2003, with 碧澜桥 Bilan Qiao and five other bridges; design drawings for presenting 坦坦荡荡 and the bridges 如意桥, 南大桥, 棕亭桥, 鸣溪桥, the one-arch bridge of 慈云普护 and 碧澜桥 were approved in 2007 (S981). The dig gave a blue-and-white porcelain stool from the 'goldfish pond' 金鱼池, restored in the 修复1860 project (E1339, S334). The pool and footings are shown in the park today; the dig report itself was not reached.
YM10.recons_en: Tsinghua news pages (search extract only, not fetched) say the 贺艳 / 郭黛姮 digital reconstruction rests on excavation data, Yangshi Lei drawings and the 烫样 models, and cite 碧澜桥 among worked examples; no study by 贺艳 specific to 坦坦荡荡 was found in this pass. See the R rows already in the catalogue for this scene.
YM10.gaps_en: The 2003 excavation report (pool size, depth, footing plan) not reached; the brief's '贺艳's study' of 坦坦荡荡 was not found; no dimension was obtained.

YM11.en: Seize the Old; It Contains the Present
YM11.what_en: 茹古涵今 Rugu Hanjin, a library court north of 长春仙馆 and south of 坦坦荡荡 (S05 j81:3b, 4b): the five-bay hall 茹古涵今 facing south, behind it the square hall 韶景轩 Shaojing Xuan of five bays on each face, 茂育斋 Maoyu Zhai east and 竹香斋 Zhuxiang Zhai west in front of it, and 静通斋 Jingtong Zhai to the north (S05 j81:3b). 韶景轩 carried a plaque on each of its four eaves: 喜接南薰 south, 景丽东皇 east, 翠生西岭 west, 清风北户 north (S05 j81:4a). Malone calls its roof double (S02 p.80, in the halls table). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM11.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "繚以曲垣綴以周廊邃館明忩牙籖萬軸" (S05 j81:4b): walled by winding walls and strung with galleries, deep halls and bright windows, ten thousand book-scrolls; the poem quotes Du Fu, 'not slighting the moderns, loving the ancients'.
YM11.gaps_en: Only S05 and S02 stand for the layout; no dig; S360 records not read in this pass.

YM12.en: The Long Spring Lodge of the Immortal
YM12.what_en: 长春仙馆 Changchun Xianguan, south of 茹古涵今, on the west side of the front lake behind 正大光明: a three-bay gate, a five-bay main hall, 绿荫轩 Lüyin Xuan behind it and 丽景轩 Lijing Xuan behind the west gallery (S05 j81:5a); west of it 含碧堂 Hanbi Tang of five bays with 林虚桂静, 古香斋, 抑斋, 墨池云 and 随安室 (E1405, S05). It was Hongli's residence as a prince from 1729; after 1735 his empress used it and the dowager stayed here at festivals; Jiaqing lived here from 1796 under the retired Qianlong (E1406, E1411, S360). It gave its name to 长春园 (E1417, S02 p.98). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM12.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "循壽山口西入屋宇深䆳重廊曲檻逶迤相接" (S05 j81:5b): entered west through the pass of 寿山, deep halls linked by double galleries and winding rails, a court with paulownias and rocks; 'my old residence, now slightly repaired, where I receive the Empress Dowager on festivals'.
YM12.later_en: Many later names: 丽景轩, 林虚桂静, 绿荫轩, 春好轩 Chunhao Xuan, 藤影花丛 Tengying Huacong all have poems by Jiaqing from 1796 (E1412-E1416, S360), when he lodged here. On S01 the five-bay main hall is labelled 藤影花丛 (YM12-02) and a seven-bay row carries the label 长春仙馆 (YM12-N01): the plan state is post-1796 and may have moved the name to another hall. 古香斋 was named after the east room of 重华宫 (E1407).
YM12.setting_en: Paulownias and rocks in the court (S05 j81:5b); magnolias at 含碧堂 (note of 1797, E1408); a stream 鸣玉溪 with a bridge pavilion (YM12-11, 卷棚歇山 per S41) and boating (E1409).
YM12.gaps_en: No dig found (search for a 长春仙馆 excavation gave nothing). Which hall bore the 长春仙馆 plaque in 1860 is unclear (Q below).

YM16.en: Dwelling of the Moon, Earth, and Clouds
YM16.what_en: 月地云居 Yuedi Yunju, a Buddhist temple north of 山高水长 across a bridge, entered through a pass in the hills: a five-bay hall, a square front hall of five bays on each face, a rear storeyed hall of seven bays on both floors; 法源楼 Fayuan Lou and a 静室 to the east; to the west, across a bridge and north, the temple of 刘猛将军 Liu Meng Jiangjun, the locust-driving god (S05 j81:18b). Plaques: gate 清净地, front hall 妙证无声, rear eave 莲花法藏 (S05 j81:19a). The garden was burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188), but 魁星楼 Kuixing Lou (YM16-08, tie 'likely') stood among the 17 buildings 刘敦桢 listed as left after the fire in 1933 (E0451, S337).
YM16.scene_en: Lyric of 1744 (to 清平乐), as written on the leaf P0016: "琳宮一區背山臨流松色翠密與紅墻相映結楞嚴壇大悲壇其中": a temple with hills behind and water in front, dense green pines against RED WALLS, with a Śūraṅgama altar and a Great Compassion altar inside. The 日下旧闻考 copy reads 紅橋 'red bridge' for 紅墻 (S05 j81:19a); the painting shows red walls round the temple, so the leaf's reading stands.
YM16.later_en: On S01 the square front hall is labelled 都罡殿 (YM16-02) and the main hall 三世佛殿 (YM16-03); S05 gives neither name. Whether these are later names or names of the images inside is open.
YM16.interior_en: Malone: a temple of the Buddha of the Three Worlds (S02 p.83), which fits the S01 label 三世佛殿 on the main hall (YM16-03). His note describes a walled court with central and side gates, a drum tower and a bell tower, a large square building with eight columns on each side and a double roof, two stele pavilions and a two-storey building at the rear (S02 p.83 n.). Eight columns a side on a hall of five bays a side (S05 j81:18b) implies a surrounding gallery: 5 bays plus a gallery bay at each end.
YM16.gaps_en: No dig; storeys of 法源楼 not stated; S02 p.83 note on the double roof of the square hall is the only roof evidence (halls table).

YM17.what_en: 鸿慈永祜 Hongci Yonghu, "Vast Compassion and Eternal Blessing", is the ancestral temple 安佑宫 Anyou Gong in the north-west of the garden, on what the 1744 preface calls its brightest and driest ground (S05 j81:24a). Begun in 1742 and finished in 1743 on the model of 寿皇殿 Shouhuang Dian (S05 j81:19b-21b, E1556; E1555; E1564, S361; E1560, S360). S05 walks it as a glazed archway with stone 华表 (four by Malone and the PKU record, E1561, S980), three more archways round it to the south, east and west, a moon-river bridge south of them, the three-bay 致孚殿 Zhifu Dian to the south-east facing west, the five-bay gate 安佑门 Anyou Men facing south behind three white marble bridges, a well pavilion and five-bay waiting rooms on each side, and inside the gate the double-eaved nine-bay hall 安佑宫 with five-bay side halls, a stele pavilion and a burner pavilion on each side (S05 j81:19b-21b, E1556). The hall had a hip-and-gable roof in yellow glazed tile (E1560, S360) and held the portraits of Kangxi in the centre and Yongzheng on the east, later joined by others (E1556; E1560; E1564). Malone describes two red walls with yellow-glazed coping, five marble bridges over the moat, two stone qilin and a marble terrace with five stairs (E1561-E1563, S02 pp.83-88). Its halls were burned with the rest of the garden by British troops on Elgin's order on 18-19 October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188); the masonry stood as a ruin until it was pulled down under the Republic (S02 p.218).
YM17.scene_en: Leaf 17 of the 1744 album (P0017). Preface of 1744: "苑西北地最爽塏爰建殿寢敬奉皇祖皇考神御以申罔極之懷" (S05 j81:24a-b): on the bright, dry ground of the garden's north-west he built halls to hold the portraits of his grandfather and father; tall pines round the wall 'stir reverence and love on sight' (望之起敬起愛); rites at new and full moon (朔望展禮). The stele text of Qianlong traces ancestral halls from antiquity and explains the nine-room hall, Kangxi in the centre and Yongzheng in the east room (E1555, S05).
YM17.later_en: In the decades after 1860 the ruin served as a quarry. Malone writes that under the Republic 王怀庆 Wang Huaiqing, commanding the Peking gendarmerie, took materials to build his own garden and let carters haul away brick and stone, and that the masonry of the Ancestral Shrine, 舍卫城 and 方壶胜境 was among what was pulled down; pieces from the shrine stood at Yenching University in his day (S02 p.218). Three of the four 华表 were moved to Yenching University in 1925 (S980).
YM17.setting_en: Yellow glazed roofs on the main hall (E1560) and yellow-glazed coping on red walls (E1563); green-glazed incense burners in the inner court (E1562); pines round the precinct (S05 j81:24b); a moat with marble bridges (E1563).
YM17.survives_en: Pieces of 安佑宫 stand at Peking University (the former Yenching): the white marble 华表, about 8 m high on octagonal bases 1.24 m high, an uneven pair, which stood before the glazed archway (S980); the stone qilin, 1.74 m high on 0.98 m bases, which had stood before 大宫门 until they were moved to 安佑宫 in 1741, came through 1860 undamaged, and were taken out late in the Qing and bought by 载涛 Zaitao, whose 朗润园 passed to Yenching (S943); and one dragon-and-cloud ramp stone 3.15 x 1.30 m, its pair at the east gate of 颐和园 (S943). In 1925 Yenching moved three of the 华表; the fourth went into the city and in 1931 lay before Tiananmen; when the Beijing Library built its new 文津 building it meant to take Yenching's spare one to pair with it, but by a mix-up neither place ended with a matched pair (S980). No dig of the temple platform has been found.
YM17.gaps_en: No excavation report of the 安佑宫 platform was found. Yangshi Lei plans or sections of 安佑宫 may exist but none is on disk. What of the platform remains in the park today is not described in any source on disk.
YM17.what_zh: 鸿慈永祜即安佑宫，是圆明园中供奉先帝御容的祖祠，位于园西北部（S05 j81:24a）。乾隆七年（1742）仿寿皇殿规制兴建，次年（1743）落成（S05; E1555; E1564）。据《日下旧闻考》，前有琉璃坊座，左右立石华表，坊南及东西又有三坊环列；其南为月河桥，东南为西向的致孚殿三楹；宫门五楹南向，为安佑门，门前白玉石桥三座，左右井亭、朝房；门内为重檐正殿九楹，即安佑宫，中龛奉康熙帝圣容，左龛奉雍正帝圣容，左右配殿各五楹，碑亭、燎亭各一（S05 j81:19b-21b, E1556）。正殿覆黄琉璃瓦（E1560）。1860年10月18日至19日英军奉额尔金之命焚园，安佑宫殿宇被毁（S02 pp.187-188）；残存砖石在民国时期被大量拆运（S02 p.218）。
YM17.survives_zh: 安佑宫的部分石构件今存北京大学（原燕京大学）：一对汉白玉华表，通高约8米，八角形须弥座高1.24米，原立于安佑宫琉璃坊前，两根粗细不一（S980）；一对石麒麟，高1.74米，座高0.98米，原在大宫门前，乾隆六年（1741）移至安佑宫，1860年未受破坏，清末被盗出后由朗润园园主载涛购得，后随朗润园归燕京大学（S943）；以及一块龙云丹陛石，长3.15米、宽1.30米，另一块在颐和园东宫门（S943）。1925年燕京大学从圆明园运走三根华表，第四根运入城内，后因搬运差错，北大与国家图书馆两处的华表都不成对（S980）。安佑宫台基尚未见考古发掘报告。
YM17.summary_en: The imperial ancestral temple of the garden, built in 1742-43 after the 寿皇殿, with the portraits of Kangxi and Yongzheng in a nine-bay hall under yellow glazed tile. Burned in October 1860; its marble columns, qilin and a ramp stone now stand at Peking University.
YM17.scene_zh: 四十景图第十七景（P0017）。乾隆九年诗序云：“苑西北地最爽塏爰建殿寢敬奉皇祖皇考神御以申罔極之懷”；又写周垣乔松“望之起敬起愛”，朔望在此行礼（S05 j81:24a-b）。乾隆《御制安佑宫碑文》追述历代宗庙、原庙之制，说明殿为九室，中奉康熙，东室奉雍正（E1555）。
YM17.summary_zh: 圆明园中的皇家祖祠，1742年至1743年仿寿皇殿建成，九间正殿覆黄琉璃瓦，供奉康熙、雍正御容；1860年10月被焚，其华表、石麒麟和丹陛石今存北京大学。

YM18.what_en: 汇芳书院 Huifang Shuyuan, east of 鸿慈永祜 beyond three ridges and a bridge: inner hall 抒藻轩 Shuzao Xuan, 涵远斋 Hanyuan Zhai behind, 翠照楼 inside the west wall, 倬云楼 Zhuoyun Lou inside the east wall, 眉月轩 Meiyue Xuan further east, 随安室 south-east of 倬云楼, an open three-bay hall 问津 Wenjin further east, and across a stream a stone archway named 断桥残雪 Duanqiao Canxue (S05 j81:25b-26a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM18.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "東偏學月牙形搆小齋數椽旁列虚亭竒石負土爭出穴洞谽谺" (S05 j81:26b): on the east a small crescent-shaped studio (the 眉月轩), open pavilions, strange rocks and caves one can climb to the stone room 问津; the poem ties the name 'gathered fragrance' to the raising of talent.
YM18.later_en: 断桥残雪 was a rough stone bridge over a stream east of the court, likened by Qianlong in 1753 to the one on West Lake (E1592, S360); 问津 is called in 1797 a rustic three-bay house on the rockery under Yongzheng's plaque (S360 compiler). Poems run to 1798.
YM18.gaps_en: S43 gives 抒藻轩 a 卷棚悬山 roof (halls table); nothing else on roofs; no dig.

YM19.what_en: 日天琳宇 Ritian Linyu, a Buddhist and Daoist temple south of 汇芳书院 modelled on the rear Buddha tower of 雍和宫 (S05 j81:27b): a middle and a west row of storeyed halls, each with a front and a rear tower of seven bays on both floors, linked by three-bay passages; a 'sky bridge' 天桥 joining the middle front tower to a double-eaved octagonal lantern pavilion 灯亭; east and west corner towers; 楞严坛 in an octagonal pavilion inside the east wall; and further east the 瑞应宫 Ruiying Gong with 仁应殿, 和感殿 and 晏安殿 for the dragon gods (S05 j81:27a-28b). Guandi upstairs in the middle front tower, the Jade Emperor upstairs in the west front tower (S05 j81:28a). 晏安殿 was nine bays from 1788, seven before (halls table). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM19.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "紫微丹地中立一化城截斷紅塵" (S05 j81:28b): a 'phantom city' of the Buddha set inside the red-walled palace, cutting off the dust of the world.
YM19.later_en: S361's editors say the towers were rebuilt in mid-Qianlong, four of seven bays on two floors, with a 太岁坛 and seven Buddha halls (E1612); 晏安殿 became nine bays in 1788 (halls table). Malone saw two-storey buildings linked at upper-floor level by a bridge and a second bridge out to a high rockery (E1610, S02).
YM19.gaps_en: No dig; the 雍和宫 model suggests 佛楼 proportions but nothing is measured.

YM21.en: Reflections on the Water and the Fragrance of Iris
YM21.what_en: 映水兰香 Yingshui Lanxiang, west of 澹泊宁静 across the river: a five-bay hall facing west, with 钓鱼矶 Diaoyu Ji to the south-east, the pool 印月池 Yinyue Chi north, 知耕织 Zhi Gengzhi north of the pool, 濯鳞沼 Zhuolin Zhao further north-east, and 贵织山堂 Guizhi Shantang to the south-west, a shrine to the silkworm god (S05 j81:33b-34a; E1666). Its pond held carp brought from Rehe (S05 j81:33b, poem on 濯鳞沼). A farm scene: rice fields in front (S05 j81:34a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM21.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "屋旁松竹交隂翛然逺俗前有水田數棱" (S05 j81:34a): pines and bamboo shade the house, a few strips of paddy in front, and the cool wind brings the scent of rice; the poem ends with the 豳风 farming pictures and the duty to the field officials.
YM21.gaps_en: S361's editors describe a farm-themed garden rebuilt in mid-Qianlong with 多稼轩 and other halls (E1670); whether that note belongs to 映水兰香 or to its neighbour 澹泊宁静 (YM20) should be checked. No dig.

YM22.en: A Stream and Trees and a Bright Lute
YM22.what_en: 水木明瑟 Shuimu Mingse, north-east of 映水兰香: a three-bay hall built across a stream, where a European water device (泰西水法) drove fans inside the room, whence the name 风扇房 (S05 j81:35a; E1686, S361; E1685, S02). 文源阁, the library of 1774, was built just north-west of it (S05 j81:35b; S02 says on the site of rice fields and a double-roofed pavilion, E1685). Plaques by Qianlong and, 一溪清水引风凉, by Yongzheng (S05 j81:35a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM22.scene_en: Lyric of 1744 (to 秋风清): "用泰西水法引入室中以轉風扇泠泠瑟瑟非絲非竹天籟遙聞" (S05 j81:35a-b): water drawn into the room by the Western method turns the fans, with a clear sound, neither string nor flute, like the music of heaven.
YM22.later_en: The 1774 文源阁 changed the neighbourhood (S05 j81:35b); S01 labels 丰乐轩 in this scene (YM22-02), but S05 puts 丰乐轩 in 紫碧山房 (E2302): a tie to check.
YM22.gaps_en: The water mechanism is not described in detail anywhere found; no dig of the stream channel.

YM23.en: The Happy Place of Falling Streams
YM23.what_en: 濂溪乐处 Lianxi Lechu, an island hall north-west of 水木明瑟, ringed by pond and stream: the nine-bay main hall (eave plaque 慎修思永 Shenxiu Siyong), 云香清胜 behind, 芰荷深处 on the east wall, the gallery 香雪廊 turning north-east, the tower 云霞舒卷 and a pavilion 临泉 (S05 j82:1a-b; E1703). To the south the flower-god temple 汇万总春之庙 with the five-bay 蕃育群芳, 香远益清楼, 乐天和, 味真书屋, 池水共心月同明 and 普济桥 (S05 j82:2a-b; E1704, E2376). S361 adds 水云居, 荷香书屋, 延云殿, a seven-bay 知过堂 and 墨光亭 (E1709). The garden was burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188), but 慎修思永 and 知过堂 (YM23-01, YM23-N01) stood among the 17 buildings 刘敦桢 listed as left after the fire in 1933 (E0451, S337).
YM23.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "苑中菡萏甚多此處特盛小殿數楹流水周環於其下" (S05 j82:1b-2a): the garden has many lotuses but here most; a small hall of a few bays with water flowing round under it; the poem names Zhou Dunyi, the lover of lotus.
YM23.later_en: Malone notes that the plan S01 lacks the long covered porch on piles round the lotus pond and the open pavilion south of the island that the leaf shows, probably removed by then (E1708, S02); S01 adds 知过堂 (YM23-N01, seven bays) and 水云居 (YM23-N03), names not in S05. So the 1860 state differs from the leaf: drop the pile gallery.
YM23.gaps_en: When the pile gallery went and 知过堂 came is not dated here (S360 may have it). No dig.

YM24.what_en: 多稼如云 Duojia Ruyun, north across the river from 濂溪乐处 facing the rice fields: a five-bay main hall with 芰荷香 Jihe Xiang as front hall and 湛绿 Zhanlü to the south-east (S05 j82:2b-3a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM24.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "坡有桃沼有蓮月地花天虹梁雲棟巍若仙居矣隔垣一方鱗塍參差" (S05 j82:3a): peaches on the slope, lotus in the pool, a hall like an immortal's dwelling; beyond the wall scale-like paddies where farmers in straw capes come and go, after the ancient 'play field' 弄田 for learning the seasons of farming.
YM24.gaps_en: Thin: 18 evidence rows; no dig, no dimension.

YM25.what_en: 鱼跃鸢飞 Yuyue Yuanfei, north-east of 多稼如云: a hall open on all four sides, each face five bays (四面為門各五楹), 畅观轩 Changguan Xuan as east wing, the tower 铺翠环流 Pucui Huanliu to the south-west, 传妙 Chuanmiao south of the tower, and 多子亭 Duozi Ting beyond the pass (S05 j82:3b-4a). Face plaques: east 岚光曙色, south 绮疏文照, north 涧溜调琴 (S05 j82:4a-b). The garden was burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188), but 鱼跃鸢飞 itself stood among the 17 buildings 刘敦桢 listed as left after the fire in 1933 (E0451, S337).
YM25.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "榱桷翼翼户牖四達曲水周遭儼如縈帶兩岸村舍鱗次" (S05 j82:4b): rafters spread like wings, doors open to all four sides, a winding stream round it like a belt, village houses in rows on both banks.
YM25.later_en: S360's compiler describes 鱼跃鸢飞 as a two-storey tower with a pyramidal roof and doors on all four sides, under Yongzheng's plaque, dominating the low buildings of the north (S360); S05 gives five bays on each face (j82:3b). It survived 1860 (E0451).

YM26.en: Village of the Distant Northern Mountains
YM26.what_en: 北远山村 Beiyuan Shancun, an imitation farm village on both banks of the river east of 鱼跃鸢飞, among fields: at the west end of the stone-walled north bank 兰野 Lanye, behind it 绘雨精舍, south-west 水村图, then a pair of linked storeyed halls, 皆春阁 Jiechun Ge in front and 稻凉楼 Daoliang Lou behind, further west 涉趣楼 and 湛虚书屋 (S05 j82:5a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM26.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "循苑牆度北闗村落鱗次竹籬茅舎巷陌交通" (S05 j82:5b): along the garden wall past the north gate, a village of thatched huts with bamboo fences and lanes, herdsmen's flutes and fishermen's songs answering the pestles; the poem lists water-wheels on the banks and a herd-boy on a buffalo.
YM26.later_en: Major change after 1744: in 1817 (Jiaqing) the five-bay 课农轩 Kenong Xuan with a three-bay annex was built on the sites of 皆春阁, 稻凉楼, 涉趣楼 and 湛虚书屋 (E1756, S361); so for 1860 the west part of 北远山村 is 课农轩 (YM51), not the linked towers of S05. Some buildings survived 1860 under guard, say the editors (E1756).
YM26.setting_en: Thatched cottages, bamboo fences, water-wheels on the banks, seedling boats in the paddies (S05 j82:5b-6a); a stone revetment on the north bank (北岸石垣, S05 j82:5a).

YM27.en: The Elegant Color of the Western Peaks
YM27.what_en: 西峰秀色 Xifeng Xiuse, south-west of 北远山村, a room on the river facing west to the Western Hills; across the river the pine-clad rock hill 小匡庐 Xiao Kuanglu with a 龙王庙 behind; east of it 含韵斋 Hanyun Zhai, then 一堂和气, and 自得轩 to the south-east; behind the wall 岚镜舫 Lanjing Fang east and 花港观鱼 west (S05 j82:6b; E1781). Of 1728 and Yongzheng's favourite residence (E1788, S361; S05 j82:8a note 皇考最愛居此); once with a stage for the Double Seventh; 含韵斋 five bays under three rolled roofs, 岚镜舫 twelve bays, 花港观鱼 a seven-bay hall over the river (E1788). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM27.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "軒楹洞達面臨翠巘西山爽氣在我襟袖後宇為含韻齋周植玉蘭十餘本" (S05 j82:7a): an open hall facing the green hills, the clear air of the Western Hills in one's sleeves; behind it 含韵斋 among a dozen magnolias. The poem recalls ten years at his father's side here.
YM27.setting_en: Magnolias round 含韵斋 (S05 j82:7a; Malone ten to twenty, E1786); an artificial rock mountain 小匡庐 across the river, named after Mount Lu (S05 j82:6b); four boathouses east of the scene (E2391).
YM27.survives_en: The brief names a dig at 西峰秀色; none was found in this pass (the digs worker covers yuanmingyuanpark.cn).

YM28.en: The Library of the Four Delights
YM28.what_en: 四宜书屋 Siyi Shuwu, east of 西峰秀色 past two pairs of boathouses, on the north bank: the five-bay 四宜书屋, main hall of 安澜园 Anlan Yuan; south-east 葄经馆, south 采芳洲, behind it 飞睇亭, north-east 绿帷舫, south-west 无边风月之阁, further south-west 涵秋堂, north 烟月清真楼, west of that 远秀山房, and across a curved bridge north 染霞楼 (S05 j82:8a-b; E1815). The plaque 四宜书屋 is Yongzheng's; Qianlong reshaped the site after the garden of the Chen family at Haining, whose name 安澜 he had granted in 1762 (壬午), and explained it as a wish for safe sea walls, Yellow River and Grand Canal (E1814, S05 安澜园记; E1819, S02). S361 says it was first called 春宇舒和 (E1820). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM28.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "春宜花夏宜風秋宜月冬宜雪居處之適也" (S05 j82:8b): spring suits flowers, summer wind, autumn the moon, winter snow; a house fit for all four seasons, among a thousand trees, with blue peaks in the distance.
YM28.later_en: The 1744 leaf shows the Yongzheng-era 四宜书屋. Qianlong's essay says that twenty years after the album the buildings needed repair, and he used the repair to rearrange the halls round 四宜书屋 'so that they match the Chen garden turn for turn' (就四宜書屋左右前後畧經位置即與陳園曲折如一無二也, E1814, S05 j82:9a); the ten poems on 安澜园 are dated 1764 (乾隆二十九年, E1809, S05 j82:10a-12a). So the 1860 model follows S05 1774 and S01, not the leaf. The Yongzheng plaque stayed (皇考御額在焉, E1809).
YM28.gaps_en: No dig found (search for 四宜书屋 安澜园 遗址 gave nothing). The Haining 安澜园 itself is gone; only texts and the leaf remain.

YM30.en: Bathe the Person and Cleanse the Heart
YM30.what_en: 澡身浴德 Zaoshen Yude, at the south-west corner of 福海: the three-bay hall 澄虚榭 Chengxu Xie facing east over the lake, 含清晖 to the south, 涵妙识 to the north, turning west 静香馆, then 解愠书屋 and, to the south-west, 旷然阁 (S05 j82:14a); north across a bridge 望瀛洲 Wang Yingzhou, then 深柳读书堂 and 溪月松风 (S05 j82:15a; E1875). S361 adds 延真院 and 溪山罨画 (E1875), both labelled on S01 (YM30-N01, N02). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM30.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "福海西壖平漪鏡淨黛蓄膏停竹嶼蘆汀極望瀰瀰" (S05 j82:14b): the west shore of 福海, ripples smooth as a mirror, bamboo islets and reed banks as far as one sees, ducks bathing and egrets flying.
YM30.later_en: S05 j82:21b says the plaque 涵虚朗鉴 'formerly hung at 澄虚榭 on the west of the lake', 澄虚榭 being this scene's main hall (S05 j82:14a). Since the 1744 leaf of 涵虚朗鉴 already places that scene on the east shore (P0036), the plaque's stay at 澄虚榭 predates 1744 and does not change this scene's 1860 state.

YM34.en: There Is Another Cave of Heaven
YM34.what_en: 别有洞天 Bieyou Dongtian, the south-east corner of 福海 behind the hill: an open five-bay hall backed by the hill and facing the river, 纳翠楼 west, 水木清华之阁 south-west and 时赏斋 north-west of it (S05 j82:18b-19a); the scene was earlier called 秀清村, entered by the water gate 水关 in the east garden wall (S05 j82:19a; E1981, S02). Begun under Yongzheng as a place of Daoist alchemy; the main hall five bays under three rolled roofs; a seven-bay stone boat 活画舫; Jiaqing added the five-bay 岩水澄华 and other halls on the south bank (E1984, S361), which S01 labels (YM34-N02 ?水澄?). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM34.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "苑牆東出水闗曰秀清村長薄疎林映帶莊墅自有塵外致" (S05 j82:19a): at the water gate in the east wall lies 秀清村, sparse woods and long thickets round a farmstead, as unworldly as the 36 grotto-heavens without their steep cliffs.
YM34.later_en: Jiaqing's additions on the south bank (岩水澄华 and others, E1984) and S01's labels 涵碧亭, ?漾楼 and 竹??山斋 (YM34-N01, N03, N04) are not in S05: the 1860 scene is larger than the leaf.
YM34.survives_en: The stone boat base survives in the park (YM34-07, S06 in the halls table); not checked in this pass.

YM35.en: The Double Mirror and the Sound of the Lute
YM35.what_en: 夹镜鸣琴 Jiajing Mingqin, on the south shore of 福海 west of 别有洞天: a double-eaved square bridge pavilion over the channel (E2003, S361), 聚远楼 Juyuan Lou to the south, 广育宫 Guangyu Gong to the east for the goddess 碧霞元君 with an archway in front and 凝祥殿 behind, then 南屏晚钟, 西山入画, 山容水态; west 湖山在望, 佳山水 and 洞里长春 (S05 j82:19b-20a). 西山入画 was rebuilt about 1763 as the five-bay 开鉴堂, later 渊渟镜澈 (E2003). Malone saw a deep well on the hill that fed the waterfall by hand (E1999, S02). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM35.scene_en: Lyric of 1744 (to 水仙子): "取李青蓮兩水夾明鏡詩意架虹橋一道上搆傑閣俯瞰澄泓" (S05 j82:20b): after Li Bai's line on two waters holding a bright mirror, a rainbow bridge with a lofty pavilion on it, a cascade from the cliff beside, striking the rocks with the sound of a lute.

YM36.what_en: 涵虚朗鉴 Hanxu Langjian: in S05 (1774+) it stands on the east shore of 福海 and is the main hall of 雷峰夕照 Leifeng Xizhao, with 惠如春 to the north-west, 寻云榭, 贻兰庭, 会心不远 north, 临众芳, 云锦墅, 菊秀松蔚, 万景天全 south (S05 j82:21a). The note says its plaque 'formerly hung at 澄虚榭 on the west of the lake and was later moved to 雷峰夕照 on the east' (S05 j82:21b). S361 dates the east-shore hall to 1738: three bays facing west, 雷峰夕照 outside, 涵虚朗鉴 inside (E2018). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM36.scene_en: Preface of 1744 as written on the album leaf P0036 (read from the image): "結宇福海之東左右雲隄紆委千章層青面前巨浸空澄一泓淨碧": 'built on the EAST of 福海', cloud-like dykes left and right, the great sheet of water in front; sun and moon rise and set over it. The 日下旧闻考 copy reads 福海之西 here (S05 j82:21b-22a): the album, the earlier and autograph-copy text, says east.
YM36.later_en: S05 (1774+) puts 涵虚朗鉴 on the east shore as the main hall of 雷峰夕照 and says its plaque 'formerly hung at 澄虚榭 on the west of the lake and was later moved' there (S05 j82:21a-b). The 1744 leaf already says 結宇福海之東 (P0036), and S361 dates the east-shore three-bay hall facing west to 1738 (E2018). So the move west to east, if real, happened before 1744, and the leaf shows the east-shore site that stood in 1860; S01 labels 涵虚朗鉴 and 雷峰夕照 there (YM36, YM36-01). S05's 福海之西 in the preface looks like a copying slip or a later edit, to be checked in another edition.
YM36.best_en: The album leaf P0036 does show the east-shore site (its own text says 福海之東), so it serves for the 1860 form, together with S05 j82:21a and S01 for the layout.

YM37.en: The Porch of the Great Gentleman
YM37.what_en: 廓然大公 Kuoran Dagong, the north-west corner of 福海 west of 平湖秋月: a seven-bay main hall with 双鹤斋 Shuanghe Zhai in front, 规月桥 to the north-west, 绮吟堂, 采芝径, 峭蒨居 beyond a rock cave, the tower 天真可佳 outside the north wall, 披云径, 启秀亭, 韵石淙, a terrace 芰荷深处 on the pool, 影山楼 beyond the wall, 环秀山房 and 临湖楼 (S05 j82:22b). Begun under Yongzheng; Qianlong's rebuild copied the 寄畅园 at Wuxi and the rockwork his Panshan villa (E2035, S361). It survived 1860 and was lost around 1900, say S361's editors (E2035): so the 1860 state stands, and the ruin date is later. 刘敦桢's 1933 list of 17 buildings left after 1860 includes 双鹤斋 (YM37-02) (E0451, S337).
YM37.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "平岡迴合山禽渚鳥逺近相呼後鑿曲池有蒲菡蓞" (S05 j82:23a-b): low ridges round about, birds calling, a winding pool dug behind with rushes and lotus; the name, 'broad and impartial', from Cheng Hao: the hill does not refuse soil, the river does not refuse streams.
YM37.gaps_en: A 1755 poem is also quoted (S05 j82:23b); the survival claim of E2035 needs a primary source (e.g. the 1860s inventories).

YM40.en: The Depth of the Vault of Heaven
YM40.what_en: 洞天深处 Dongtian Shenchu, west and a little south of 如意馆, in the south-east of the garden: in front the 四所, four courts of the princes' lodgings on two east-west lanes and one north-south lane, with 福园门 Fuyuan Men before them; west of them the princes' school with 前垂天贶, 中天景物 and 后天不老 on an axis and 斯文在兹 on the east, which held a shrine of Confucius (S05 j82:28b-29a; E2089, S361). 如意馆 was the court painters' workshop where Castiglione and Attiret worked (E2089). Malone puts 福园门 in the outer wall about 300 yards east of 大宫门 (E0385, E2088, S02). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
YM40.scene_en: Preface of 1744: "縁溪而東徑曲折如蟻盤短椽陿室於奥為宜" (S05 j82:29b): along the stream eastward the path winds like an ant's spiral; small rooms with short rafters suit the deep corner; a little south is 前垂天贶, 'my brothers' and my old reading room', named by Yongzheng. He ends: 'may I be a gentleman-scholar, not a wanderer'.
YM40.later_en: S01 labels 乐道堂 (YM40-N01) and 东所 (YM40-N02), not in S05: later residents' names. 63 rows in the inventory, the most of any scene here, mostly unnamed courtyard ranges of the 四所. The gate is written 福元门 on S01 and 福园门 in the texts; a Yangshi Lei plan (sheet 043-002) names the place 福元四所, so the plan form is itself Qing (E0382, S337). Malone says the woodcut of scene 40 shows the gate and the painting does not (E0385, S02). S360 has only a short undated note (E2092).
YM40.gaps_en: No dig found; the 四所 courts need a Yangshi Lei plan (they were standard 四合院 ranges).
YM40.role_en: The Palace School, the Princes' Residences, and Studios

YM47.en: Ts'ao Yuan, Garden of Aquatic Grasses
YM47.what_en: 藻园 Zao Yuan, west of 长春仙馆 beyond the south-west gate, in the south-west corner of the garden: the five-bay 旷然堂 Kuangran Tang, 贮清书屋 behind, 夕佳书屋 on the pool east of it, 镜澜榭 a little north, the tower 凝眺 and 怀新馆 south-east, 湛碧轩 north-west, 湛清华 south-west (S05 j81:8b-9a). Not one of the Forty Scenes; Malone found a brick dated 1751 on the site (E2258, S02), and S361 dates it to about mid-Qianlong, adding 溜琴亭, 自远轩, a thirteen-bay boat dock with a route to 畅春园, and 粹藻楼 (E2259). The garden was burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188), but a building of the scene (E0451 ties it 'sure'; 藏舟坞 Cangzhou Wu, the boat dock, is the likely one) stood among the 17 buildings 刘敦桢 listed as left after the fire in 1933 (E0451, S337).
YM47.later_en: S360's compiler calls 藻园 a staging point between the garden and the western parks, mostly small studies and open halls; dated poems 1759-1798 for 藻园, 怀新馆, 夕佳书屋, 旷然堂, 晴望楼, 履吉斋 (S360). 怀新馆 faces north in the south court of 凝眺楼 (S360).
YM47.survives_en:
The 1994 auger survey by the 北京市文物研究所 ahead of a planned miniature-park scheme found the 藻园 buildings ranged round a boat dock in an L-shaped zone about 105 m N-S by 95 m E-W; the same campaign covered 十三所 and 山高水长 (S156).

Surveyed and cleared in 1994 (S981, S156): the buildings lie round a boat dock in an L plan of about 105 m north-south by 95 m east-west (E2263, S156).

YM48.what_en: 紫碧山房 Zibi Shanfang, north-west of the rear wall of 鸿慈永祜, on the highest hill of the garden: front hall 横云堂 Hengyun Tang, 石帆室 in a rock cave east of the main hall, 丰乐轩 south-east, 霁华楼 north, 景晖楼 further east, 澄素楼 on the pool west of 横云堂, 引溪亭 north-west (S05 j81:25a). Enlarged about 1760; 景晖楼 three storeys; main hall five bays with eave plaque 乐在人和; after 1860 the inner gate, the main hall and a pavilion survived under guard and were lost around 1900 (E2315, S361; S05 j81:25b). Malone's Han Shan 'Cold Hill', climbed on the ninth of the ninth moon (E2314, S02). 刘敦桢's 1933 list of 17 buildings left after 1860 includes 紫碧山房 and 顺木天 (E0451, S337).
YM48.later_en: Enlarged in 1760 after the second southern tour (E2316, E2315); a Jiaqing note of 1817 puts it in the north-west corner over the rice fields, with new barracks added near it in 1814 (S360, under 澄素楼).
YM48.survives_en:
The 2017 dig at 紫碧山房, the high north-west corner of the garden, found the duty rooms, gate, main hall, 含余清 and 澄素楼, a landing stage, a stone bridge, walls, paths, the stream, the hill and drains, and features no text records: an earlier wall base, hill retaining walls, a half-round landing and flagstone paths (S132). No figures in metres published in what was seen.

Dug in 2017: a service house, the gate, the halls 紫碧山房, 含余清 and 澄素楼, a landing, a stone bridge, walls, roads, a channel and the hill, plus an earlier wall footing, a hill retaining wall and a semicircular landing not in the documents (E2318, S132).

YM49.what_en: 若帆之阁 Ruofan zhi Ge, north-east of 北远山村 across a stone bridge and west: 湛虚翠轩, 耕云堂, then 若帆之阁, with a 关帝庙 some tens of paces east of 湛虚翠轩 (S05 j82:6a). The tower had two plaques, 御风泠然 below and 平临天境 above (S05 j82:6a-b), so two storeys. Begun 1764 inside the great north gate; S361 names the square two-storey three-bay tower 安止楼, a half-in-water pavilion 碧澜亭, 耕云堂 on a rockery and 爽籁居; 耕云堂 survived 1860 and was lost around 1900 (E2337).

YM50.what_en: 三潭印月 Santan Yinyue, north-west of 方壶胜境 on 福海's north-east, named after the West Lake view; further north-west across a bridge 天宇空明 with 澄景堂 behind, 清旷楼 east and 华照楼 west (S05 j82:13b-14a). The 方壶胜境 preface: 'to the east 蕊珠宫, to the west 三潭印月, clear and bright' (S05 j82:13a). S361 places it beside the 方壶胜境 temple garden (E1852). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

YM51.what_en: 课农轩 Kenong Xuan, built in 1817 (Jiaqing) as a five-bay hall with a three-bay annex on the sites of 皆春阁, 稻凉楼, 涉趣楼 and 湛虚书屋 of 北远山村 (E1756, S361). Not in S05 (1774+), as expected. Parts of the village survived 1860 under guard (E1756). 刘敦桢's 1933 list of 17 buildings left after 1860 includes 课农轩 (E0451, S337).
YM51.gaps_en: Only S361's editors' note found; the 1817 record and any plan should be in S360; no dig.

YM55.what_en: 后湖 Hou Hu, the Back Lake, the core water of Yuanming Yuan, ringed by the nine islands: 九洲清晏 on the south (E1153, S02), and round it 镂月开云, 天然图画, 碧桐书院, 慈云普护, 上下天光, 杏花春馆, 坦坦荡荡 and 茹古涵今, in the order S05 describes them (S05 j80:26a-j81:5a). The lake survives with its shape and has been re-dug and lined (S146, S148).
YM55.gaps_en: No figure for the lake's depth or shore construction in 1860; the shore today is a modern lining.

CC02.what_en: 含经堂 Hanjing Tang, "Hall Holding the Classics", is the largest group of 长春园 Changchun Yuan, on the central island (E0494, E0057; Malone's No.2, E0056). The hall was new in 1747 (E0014, E0015, E0057). 日下旧闻考 Rixia Jiuwen Kao walks it from 云容水态 Yunrong Shuitai north-west by a hill path: three glazed 坊楔 arches, a five-bay south-facing gate, the seven-bay 含经堂, then 淳化轩 Chunhua Xuan (printed 淳化閣 in the list, 淳化軒 in the note) and 蕴真斋 Yunzhen Zhai on the axis, with 霞翥楼 Xiazhu Lou and 渊映斋 Yuanying Zhai to the east and 梵香楼 Fanxiang Lou and 涵光室 Hanguang Shi to the west (S05 j83:4a-4b; E0052). In 1770, his sixtieth year, Qianlong rebuilt the north part as the home he meant to retire to in the sixtieth year of his reign (E0401): he had the 淳化阁帖 recut and the slabs set in the existing galleries behind 含经堂, moved 蕴真斋 a little north and enlarged its old base into the hall 淳化轩 (S05 j83:5a-5b, E0051; E0055); 蕴真斋, 三友轩 Sanyou Xuan, 静莲斋 Jinglian Zhai, 待月楼 Daiyue Lou and 理心楼 Lixin Lou date from the same campaign (E0057). 霞翥楼, inner plaque 味腴书屋, was shelved for a set of the 四库全书荟要 (E0052, E0053, E0057); 梵香楼 opposite held some 700 Buddhist images (E0061). A shop street 买卖街 Maimai Jie ran outside the east wall (S940 p.360; E2156; S990). Like the rest of the gardens it was looted by French and British troops on 6-8 October 1860 and burned by British troops on Elgin's order on 18-19 October (S02 pp.179-188; S940 p.359); guards were still posted on the site after 1860 (E0057). The site was excavated in 2001-2003 (S990; E0062).
CC02.later_en: The 1770 works changed the compound most: 淳化轩, 蕴真斋 and the west court with 三友轩 are of the 1770 campaign (E0057), and a note of 1771 says the galleries were done but the stones not yet carved (E0055). Jiaqing added a stage east of 淳化轩 in 1814 (E0057): the two-storey 乐奏钧天 Yuezou Juntian, facing the hall 神心妙达 Shenxin Miaoda, which was rebuilt in mid-Jiaqing as a five-bay viewing hall (S940 p.360). This fits the pasted slip of 1814 on the Yangshi Lei plan titled 长春园淳化轩, drawn after 1794 (E0060). Dated poems run on to 1810 at 含经堂 and to 1824 (Daoguang) at 淳化轩 (E0053, E0050, E0055). Malone repeats hearsay that Qianlong retired here after his abdication (E0056); the Qing texts read here record only the plan (E0401; S940 p.362).
CC02.interior_en: 淳化轩: inner plaque 奉三无私, couplet 貞石麗延廊畧存古意 / 淳風扇寰宇冀遂初心, and the recut 淳化阁帖 stones set in the walls of the east and west galleries (S05 j83:4b; E0052). 蕴真斋: inner plaque 礼园书圃; 霞翥楼: inner plaque 味腴书屋, and the 四库全书荟要 on shelves fitted like those of 摛藻堂 in the palace (a note of 1777, E0053; E0052, E0057). 梵香楼: a Buddhist tower of some 700 images; a small bronze inscribed 地天母, found in the dig, is identified by the park's archaeologist as the only one known to survive (E0061).
CC02.setting_en: A forecourt south of the gate with three glazed arches on its east, south and west sides, crossing stone paths, carved-brick paving, foundations for yurts (毡帐) and planting pits; a Taihu-stone rockery in front of the 淳化轩 terrace; a piled-rock hill round 三友轩 in the west court (S990 contents; S940 p.360). Open halls on the water outside the walls: 澄波夕照 Chengbo Xizhao to the west and 得胜概 Desheng Gai behind the north gate (S940 p.360; S990; E0063). Malone's plate p.100 shows a rock garden north of it (E0056). Roofs come from S940, from texts and the ruin, not from a picture: 含经堂 a seven-bay double-eaved hip-and-gable hall (S940 p.360; S361 also calls it glazed, E0057), 淳化轩 hip-and-gable, rolled on p.360 and glazed on p.361, 渊映斋, 涵光室 and 静莲斋 five-bay hip-and-gable halls, and 待月楼 a three-bay hip-and-gable tower of two storeys (S940 p.360).
CC02.survives_en: The whole 含经堂 compound was dug in 2001-03 by the 北京市文物研究所 team led by 靳枫毅 (S143; S990) and is shown as a consolidated ruin; the cleared site was presented by December 2003 (E0061). The brief's abstract, as reported in a library record, counts over 60,000 m2 of site, over 30,000 m2 of building remains and more than 30 building units (S143, E0062); the full report of 2006 describes every unit by name (S990). Measured on the ruin: 三友轩 11.1 x 7.2 m on a platform 11.9 x 8.3 m (S940 p.364). About twenty underfloor heating systems (地炕) survive with stokeholes, fireboxes and centipede-pattern flues; the largest stokehole, 2.37 x 1.8 m, is at 蕴真斋 (S940 pp.367-368). The stage 乐奏钧天 is about 16 m square over a granite cellar 2.47 m high (E0064, citing the brief). The shop row east of the wall left a base 135.65 m long, with 40 shop bays in 9 units and 28 stoves (E2156; S941, both citing S143); its width is given as about 6.3 m (E2156) and as about 63 m (S941), so it is open. The foundations of 澄波夕照, 得胜概 and a rock pavilion are reported to have been partly restored (E0063). The full brief and the 2006 report are not seen.
CC02.recons_en: Modern readings: the Tsinghua/清城睿现 AR guide (R0042), a model photograph and plan figures in 王文涛 Wang Wentao 2015 (R0316, R0317, S940), the dig drawings of S143/S990 (R0318) and, as a blog reports, a reconstruction board at the site (R0319). 王文涛 builds on the dig and the Yangshi Lei plan 长春园淳化轩 and compares 淳化轩 with 乐寿堂 Leshou Tang in the Forbidden City, which a Qing note says copied it (S940 p.362).
CC02.best_en: For modellers: S990 (the full dig report, to request) and S940 (bays, roofs and one measured hall); the Yangshi Lei plan E0060 (catalogue record only, no image here); the excavated platforms on the 2013 photographs (P0403-P0410, P0505). 乐寿堂 in the 宁寿宫 Ningshou Gong, said by a Qing note to copy 淳化轩 (S940 p.362), is the nearest standing comparable for 淳化轩: a twin, not evidence for its size.
CC02.gaps_en: No measured footprint of 含经堂, 淳化轩 or 蕴真斋 is on disk: they are in S990 chapter 3 and S143, neither seen. Roofs are stated only in S940 and S361, from texts and the ruin, and disagree for 淳化轩 (rolled or glazed); storeys are stated only for 待月楼 (two, S940 p.360); for 霞翥楼, 梵香楼 and 理心楼 two storeys are read from the name 楼 alone. The width of the shop street is open (6.3 or 63 m). The Yangshi Lei plan 样021-23 (E0060) is not viewed. No period picture: the compound is not in any album.
CC02.what_zh: 含经堂是长春园中规模最大的一组建筑，位于园中部的大岛上（E0494, E0057）。含经堂建成于乾隆十二年（1747）（E0014, E0057）。据《日下旧闻考》，自云容水态西北循山径入，有琉璃坊楔三座，其北为五间南向宫门，内为七间含经堂，后为淳化轩、蕴真斋；堂东为霞翥楼、渊映斋，堂西为梵香楼、涵光室（S05 j83:4a-4b; E0052）。乾隆三十五年（1770），乾隆帝重刻淳化阁帖，嵌于含经堂后旧有回廊，并将蕴真斋稍向北移，在旧基上拓建淳化轩，作为日后归政颐养之所（E0401, E0051, E0055）。霞翥楼贮《四库全书荟要》（E0057）。东墙外有买卖街（S940 p.360）。1860年10月6日至8日，英法联军劫掠圆明园；10月18日至19日，英军奉额尔金之命焚园，含经堂亦在其中（S02 pp.179-188）。2001年至2003年遗址经全面发掘（S990; E0062）。
CC02.survives_zh: 2001年至2003年，北京市文物研究所（靳枫毅等）对含经堂遗址进行了全面发掘，现以整修后的遗址展示（S143; S990; E0061）。据简报摘要，遗址面积六万余平方米，建筑遗迹三万余平方米，共三十余个单元（S143, E0062）。三友轩遗址实测面阔约11.1米、进深约7.2米，台面约11.9×8.3米（S940 p.364）。遗址中保存有近二十处地炕，均为“蜈蚣道”式火道，蕴真斋烧火坑最大，长2.37米、宽1.8米（S940 pp.367-368）。乐奏钧天戏台约16米见方，下有花岗岩地下室，净高2.47米（E0064）。东墙外买卖街基址南北长135.65米，有铺面40间、炉灶28座；其东西宽度一说约6.3米（E2156），一说约63米（S941），尚待核实。
CC02.summary_en: The largest group of Changchun Yuan, built in 1747 and rebuilt from 1770 as the retirement home Qianlong planned, with the recut 淳化阁帖 stones in its galleries. Looted and burned in October 1860, fully excavated in 2001-03 and shown as a ruin.
CC02.summary_zh: 长春园最大的建筑群，乾隆十二年建成，乾隆三十五年起改建为预备归政后颐养之所；1860年被劫掠焚毁，2001年至2003年全面发掘，现为遗址。

CC14.what_en: 玉玲珑馆 Yulinglong Guan, "Hall of Exquisite Jade", stood on an island south of 狮子林 (S05 j83:17a; E0288). 日下旧闻考 gives the main range 正谊明道 of five bays, 林光澹碧 to the north (inner plaque 逰心於淡), 鹤安斋 to the east and 蹈和堂 to the south-west (E0288). Built 1747 and added to about 1764 (E0291). S361 describes a five-bay gate, the main hall 正谊明道 (it says seven bays against five in S05), a nine-bay rear hall 林光澹碧, a west court with 撷景室, 蹈和堂 and the square 朝晖亭 on the water, and an east court with the five-bay 鹤安斋, the double-eaved 狎鸥亭, 随安室, a greenhouse, a fountain, 澹然书屋 and 芥舟 on the shore (E0291). Cranes were kept and released at 鹤安斋 (E0289); the poems speak of Taihu rocks, bamboo and summer visits by boat (E0267, E0290). The name lasts in poems to 1807 (E0290). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
CC14.survives_en: Scattered foundations only, in the park's status table of about 2011 (E2000); one ruin photograph of 2013 (P0457). No dig found.
CC14.gaps_en: No measured size; the Yangshi Lei base plan 样式雷排架070-1 (E0292) is not viewed. Bays of 正谊明道 differ: five in S05, seven in S361.

CC04.what_en: 思永斋 Siyong Zhai, "Studio of Long Reflection", stood north of the stream behind 蒨园: a seven-bay hall, gate plaque 静便趣 and inner plaque 萬横香玉, with the tower 山色湖光共一楼 over the water to the north and the side court 小有天园 to the east (S05 j83:9a-9b; E0135). Begun 1747 on a ringed island (E0138). Qianlong wrote in 1785 that it had stood over twenty years, older than 宁寿宫, and like it was meant for his retirement (E0136). The east court copies 小有天园, the 汪 family garden at 南屏, Hangzhou, named on the tour of 1751 and seen again in 1757: rockwork as 慧日峰, a tin-roofed room, a cascade and small Huangshan pines (S05 j83:9b-10b, E0134; Malone E0137). S361 adds an octagonal gallery to the tower and copies of the recut 淳化阁帖 and of the 西洋楼 engravings kept inside (E0138). Poems run to 1831 (E0136). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
CC04.setting_en: 小有天园: in a room ten 笏 square with a window half that, rocks piled as a peak (慧日), a room roofed in tin (範錫為宇), a cascade, Huangshan pines among stone shoots (S05 j83:9b-10b: 範錫為宇又依然壑庵也 ... 激水作瀑). Blue-and-white tiles from 思永斋 were among the restored dig finds of 2019 (E1339), so some walls or floors were faced in porcelain tile.
CC04.survives_en: Ruin photographs of 2013 show the hall site, the 小有天园 court and a fish pond (P0411, P0412, P0445, P0446). Blue-and-white tiles from the site are in the park's restoration programme (E1339). No dig report found.

CC06.what_en: 海岳开襟 Haiyue Kaijin, "Open Breast to Sea and Mountain", was a three-storey building on a round raised base in the pool north of 思永斋, with an arch on each of the four sides (S05 j83:11a: 中有圓式崇基其上樓宇三層為海嶽開襟四旁枋楔各一; E0145). Finished 1747 (E0164, S991). Plaques: 海岳开襟 inside the lower storey, 青瑶屿 on the south eave, 乘六龙 on the top storey (S05 j83:11a); the park adds 得沧洲趣 for the middle storey (S991). The park's text gives the main tower five bays a side below with double-eaved porches and three bays a side on the two upper storeys, double-eaved halls north and south, four double-eaved square pavilions, 36 bays of curved gallery and four arches, on an island with stone revetment, white marble balustrade, a landing on each side and 24 lacebark pines (S991; Malone's round terraced island with four flights of steps, E0163). The island was about 90 m across (E0164, E0165). It survived the burning of 1860 in mid-lake, was visited by Guangxu and Cixi, and was taken apart in 1900 (S991; E0164, E0451).
CC06.later_en: The group was cut down under Jiaqing and Daoguang (S991, no date or document given); repairs of 1778 and 1791 are recorded (E0165). A photograph of about 1882 by the Comte de Semallé shows the main hall then as a single-storey hall with a single-eaved pyramidal roof (S991): so the three-storey tower of S05 may not have stood in 1860. Under Guangxu a long timber bridge was added on the west shore (S991). Jiaqing still climbed 'the tower' in 1797 and 1816 (E0162, E0152).
CC06.survives_en: Taken apart in 1900 by Banner looters after months of resistance by the eunuch guards, and its trees felled; troops dug pits for treasure in the 1920s (S991). The round island was cleared of rubble in 1993 and its stone revetment re-laid; lotus ponds surround it today (S991). A totem park stood on it 1995-2007 (E0165). Ruin photographs P0413, P0414, P0503.
CC06.gaps_en: The state of 1860 is uncertain: three storeys in S05 (1780s) against one storey on the c.1882 photograph (S991). The Semallé photograph itself is not on disk. No measured diameter of the round base.

CC13.what_en: 狮子林 Shizi Lin, "Lion Grove", in the north-east of Changchun Yuan, is two gardens: 丛芳榭 of 1747 on the lake (a five-bay hall with 琴清斋 behind it) and, to its east, the copy of the Suzhou 狮子林 finished in 1772 (E0223, E0165). Qianlong based it on 倪瓒's scroll and on the Suzhou garden, then owned by a 黄 family, with rockwork by Suzhou craftsmen (S05 j83:13b-15b; E0203). 日下旧闻考 lists its parts in order: 虹桥, 假山, 纳景堂, 清閟阁, 藤架, 磴道, 占峰亭, 清淑斋, 小香幢, 探真书屋, 延景楼, 云林石室, 横碧轩, 水门 (S05 j83:13b; E0220). He named eight scenes, then eight more, sixteen in all (E0219, E0218), and kept his copy of Ni Zan's painting in 清閟阁 (E0223). Jiaqing and Daoguang wrote on the sixteen scenes again; it was partly rebuilt in 1828, the dowager dined here in 1828-29 and the last entries are of 1858 (E0221, E0223). In 1856 the emperor gave seven officials a meal at 清淑斋 (E1524). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
CC13.scene_en: Not one of the Forty Scenes, but its own set: the 狮子林十六景 named by Qianlong in 1772-73, eight and then eight more (E0203, E0218, E0219), written again in 1775, 1779, 1781, 1786 and 1793, by Jiaqing in 1796 and Daoguang in 1828 (E0221). The Chengde copy (文园狮子林) bears the same names (E0219). He owns that the pines are young and that the Suzhou garden no longer matches Ni Zan's picture (E0218).
CC13.survives_en: Ruin photographs of 2013 show the rainbow bridge and the water gate restored on their sites and the ruins of the east part (P0415, P0416, P0500, P0443). No dig report found in this round's searches.
CC13.gaps_en: Only two of the 14 named parts have a plan size (清閟阁 7 bays, 探真书屋); the rockery's form rests on the Suzhou garden and the Chengde copy, which are comparables, not evidence. No Yangshi Lei plan of the compound is in the catalogue.

CC18.what_en: 如园 Ru Yuan, "Garden of Likeness", in the south-east corner of Changchun Yuan, south-west of 鉴园 (S05 j83:18b; E0354). Finished in 1767 (E0358); early poems of 1768-70 call it 含芳书屋, the name 如园 appears from 1770 (E0356). Qianlong's poem of 1770 says its plan broadly follows the 瞻园 in the provincial treasury at 江宁 Nanjing, old garden of 徐达: 江寕藩司署中瞻園即明中山王徐逹西園之舊是園規制略倣之 (S05 j83:18b-19a; E0342); a covered way crossed the road over a double wall to 熙春园 on the south (E0342, E0356). 日下旧闻考: a three-bay gate facing west, 敦素堂, 冠霞阁 north-east of it and 明漪楼 further east; a hill path leads west to the east gate of 澹怀堂 (S05 j83:18b; E0354). Under Qianlong a piled hill split it into east and west courts, with 深宁堂 the main hall of the east court (S362). Jiaqing rebuilt it heavily, finished 1811, keeping the plan but adding winding galleries and pavilions and renaming every building except 新赏室: 深宁堂 became 延清堂; he chose ten views, the 如园十景, carved on stones beside them (S362; E0355, E0358). Daoguang and Xianfeng kept that layout, repairing rocks, shores and fittings (S362); Daoguang brought the dowager here for meals (E0356). Looted and burned in October 1860; the dig found 延清堂's floor bricks reddened and cracked through, and paths and hills reddened, from a long fire (S362; E0361).
CC18.scene_en: Not in the Forty Scenes. After the rebuilding of 1811 Jiaqing chose the 如园十景, wrote a poem on each and had them carved on stones set beside the views (S362; E0358); the 2016-17 dig fixed the places of several (E0362). The ten names are in S361 (E0358), not listed on disk.
CC18.later_en: The 1811 rebuilding is the state of 1860 here, not the Qianlong garden (S362). S362 compares four plans: 如园地盘全样 (NLC, 圆明园卷续编 第八函 p.25), 长春园全图准底 (1814-1858), the 三园地盘河道全图 of about 1873 (Palace Museum) and the 1933 遗址形势图: Tongzhi may have made small repairs (the 挹霞亭 and 待月台 bases, the rockery west of 延清堂, the 镜香池 outlet) and removed a hexagonal pavilion north of the earth hill (S362). After 1911 rocks, stone and bricks were carried off; under the Japanese occupation farmers levelled hills and filled water for rice (S362).
CC18.interior_en: 延清堂: the front bay of the first range without columns (减柱造) to give an open hall; the second range's side rooms closed by 碧纱橱, the west end room with a bed and hollow famille-rose tiles filled with sand on the floor; the third range cut into small closed rooms with beds (S362, from the Yangshi Lei interior plan). Under Jiaqing a 锦欢门幡 and a painted panel over a door are recorded (S362). Under Qianlong 深宁堂 had four flower paintings of the seasons and two trompe-l'oeil wall paintings 通景大画 (archive quoted in S362).
CC18.survives_en:
如园 was dug in two phases: 2012-13 for 芝兰室, 云萝山馆 and 听泉榭, and from November 2016 for 延清堂 and the hill paths; burning shows across the whole garden, and part is kept unexcavated (S330; E0363). From the dig and his own survey, 周秋彤 gives 延清堂 as a base 25.344 x 22.464 m and 1 m high, five bays of 4.16 and 3.84 m with a 1.664 m gallery round, three depth rows of 5.12, 6.4 and 5.12 m, a south terrace 19.68 x 7.968 m, a north terrace 12.3 x 9.3 m and a landing stage to the north (S362 sect. 三). Floors were 金砖 with a panel of hollow famille-rose tiles; roof tiles found are grey (S362).

Dug by 北京市文物研究所 in 2012 (west part; 芝兰室, 云萝山馆, 听泉榭) and 2016-2017 (second phase, with 延清堂) (S362; E0363). Site about 19,000 m2, buildings 2,800 m2, 3,800 m2 opened; 芝兰室, 云萝山馆, 听泉榭, 延清堂, 含碧楼, 挹霞亭, 观丰榭, 引胜轩, rockery, paths and shores found (E0363); over a thousand finds, among them a stone with a Jiaqing inscription, 金砖 floor bricks and famille-rose tiles, and several of the ten views placed (E0362). At 延清堂 27 of 50 column bases remain; the north terrace lies under the park's ring road and was not dug (S362).
CC18.recons_en: 周秋彤's restoration study of 延清堂 (R0015; plan R0080, section R0081, elevation R0059, interior R0060) is built from the 2016-17 dig, three Yangshi Lei sheets (065-0002-02, 065-0004-01/-02) and the 奏销档, with roof pitches taken by analogy with 景福宫 and 景福阁 (S362): use its figures, not its drawings. The Central Academy of Fine Arts' digital 如园 (R0075, 2020; video R0074) states no method on disk.
CC18.gaps_en: Only 延清堂 has a published measured reconstruction (S362, R0015, R0080, R0081, R0059). The other halls of the dig (芝兰室, 云萝山馆, 听泉榭, 含碧楼) have no published sizes on disk; the Yangshi Lei sheets 样065-0002/0004 (E0360) are cited, not seen. Names on S01 at CC18 (延清堂) are Jiaqing's, which is right for 1860.

CC16.what_en: 鉴园 Jian Yuan, "Mirror Garden", lay east of 映清斋 on the long lake north-east of 如园 (S05 j83:18a; E0307, E0324). 日下旧闻考: an open five-bay range facing west, 漱琼斋 to the north, 师善堂 east of it, and a boathouse behind (S05 j83:18a: 鑑園敞宇五楹西嚮北為潄瓊齋其東為師善堂 ... 鑑園之後有船塢). Of 1767, after 趣园 at Yangzhou; S361 adds 开益轩 north, 芳晖楼 and 绿净榭 south (E0324). Repaired in 1810 (E0165). Seven short visits in poems, 1773-1811, all on the water view (E0323). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
CC16.survives_en: In 2015 the 鉴园 site, in the south-east of Changchun Yuan against the east wall, had had no archaeological work and no protection; its remains lay in the open, mostly standing in water, scattered and overgrown (S592, Xiaoqi 2015, CC BY 3.0, section 3.1).
CC16.gaps_en: No picture, dig or Yangshi Lei plan on disk; the long boathouse (CC16-04, 46 m on S01) is the one big form. The Yangzhou 趣园 is a comparable, not evidence.

CC15.what_en: 映清斋 Yingqing Zhai, "Studio of Reflected Clarity", south-east of the pavilion 昭旷亭, which stands south of 玉玲珑馆 (S05 j83:18a; E0307). Added in 1766 as a new residence of 玉玲珑馆 (E0165). S361 describes a water garden: a fan-shaped nine-bay study with water on three sides and curved galleries, the open hall 月香水影, the five-bay two-storey 晴望楼, 益思堂, 陶嘉书屋, 豁如室 and the double-eaved square 昭旷亭 (E0308). Poems 1766-1776 (E0302-E0306). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
CC15.gaps_en: An undated ink plan 样070-9-1 (E0309) and three more titles (E1086) are not viewed; Tsinghua's render R0021 is not evidence. The fan-shaped hall is unusual: its curve should come from a plan, not a guess.

CC09.what_en: 宝相寺 Baoxiang Si, a Buddhist temple east of 法慧寺 on the north side of Changchun Yuan (S05 j83:12a; E0171). 日下旧闻考: gate facing south, then 澄光阁, then 昙霏阁, then on a raised base the hall 现大圆镜, inner plaque 香臺華鬘 (S05 j83:12a). Finished 1747; S361 gives the five-bay tower 澄光阁 with side halls 云窦 and 松关, and the five-bay 现大圆镜 on a high terrace with a three-bay annex (E0179). A Qianlong presentation plan of both temples exists (样069-1, E0175). Jiaqing visited in 1796-1801 (E0176-E0178); the emperor took officials through it in 1856 (E1524). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
CC09.gaps_en: No picture, no dig, no size beyond S01. Plan 样069-1 (E0175) not viewed.

CC08.what_en: 法慧寺 Fahui Si, a Buddhist temple on the south slope of the ridge north of 海岳开襟, west of 宝相寺 (S05 j83:12a; E0171, E0173). 日下旧闻考: gate facing west (plaque 普香界), the 四面延楼, the rear hall 光明性海, and in a west court a glazed square pagoda (S05 j83:12a: 其西别院有琉璃方塔). Finished 1747; S361 gives a five-bay main hall, a five-bay rear-facing tower with eleven-bay wings (the 四面延楼), and the pagoda as seven tiers, square below and round above, 23.55 m high (E0174). The use of eunuchs as monks here ended in 1839 (E1261, E0173). The emperor visited in 1856 (E1524). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188); the glazed pagoda stood until 1900 according to an old man Malone spoke to (E0172).
CC08.gaps_en: The pagoda is the only tall form of this part of the garden; its height 23.55 m (S361) has no stated basis on disk. R0323 cites an NLC elevation 法慧寺琉璃塔立样图: not viewed. The temple plan 样069-1 (E0175) is not viewed. No pre-1900 photograph of the pagoda found.

CC10.what_en: 泽兰堂 Zelan Tang, on the south slope of the northern hill, east of 宝相寺 through a walled gate (城关), south of the 大水法 of the Xiyang Lou (S05 j83:12b; E0186, E0187). 日下旧闻考: 翠交轩 with the stone grotto 熙春洞 under it, 爱山楼 north of it (upper plaque 天風海濤, lower 山静雲閒), and 泽兰堂 further north (plaque 神觀蕭爽) (S05 j83:12b). Begun 1746 and known for its rockwork; 泽兰堂, a five-bay hall on a high terrace, and 理性居 were added in 1759; used as a study with the best view over the fountains (E0187). A plan of July 1835 records approval to remove 理性居 and its corridors and fit railings instead (样076-3, E0188): so 理性居 was gone in 1860. Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).
CC10.later_en: 1835: 理性居 and its corridors at 泽兰堂 removed and replaced by railings (E0188). The model of 1860 should leave 理性居 out.

CC01.what_en: 澹怀堂 Danhuai Tang, Changchun Yuan's audience hall inside the south gate (Malone's No.1): a five-bay gate with five-bay court rooms east and west, the main hall 澹怀堂 (also 勤政殿, for government and feasts of frontier princes), 众乐亭 behind, the open five-bay 云容水态 across the stream and 长桥 to the south-west (S05 j83:3a-3b; E0003, E0005, E0006). Finished 1747, repaired 1769 and 1791 (E0006). The gate quarter was dug in 2001, 2003 and 2004: about 21,000 m2, 220 by 90 m, 210 trenches and 24 building remains, the layout still that of the Qianlong founding, symmetrical from screen wall to 众乐亭 with a boat landing north of it (S316 snippet; E0007, E0336). The gate was rebuilt on its site and opened in October 2016 (E0008). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

CC03.what_en: 蒨园 Qian Yuan, west of 澹怀堂 among stream and rocks, with a west-facing gate, the three-bay 朗润斋, 湛景楼, 菱香沜, the rock 青莲朵 (brought from the old 德寿宫 at Hangzhou), 标胜亭, 别有天, 韵天琴, 委宛藏, and a stele pavilion holding the recut 梅石碑 (S05 j83:7a-8a; E0103, E0092). Begun 1752, eight scenes named in 1753 (E0091, E0104); its south-east was much rebuilt about 1808 with the five-bay 碧静堂 and four new scenes named by Jiaqing in 1809 (E0104, E0105), on an ink plan of 1808 (样067-1, E0106). The 1808 state, not the 1753 one, stood in 1860.
CC03.scene_en: Not in the Forty Scenes. Qianlong named eight views of 蒨园 in 1753 (朗润斋, 湛景楼, 菱香沜, 青莲朵, 别有天, 韵天琴, 标胜亭, 委宛藏; S05 j83:8a-9a, E0091, E0104); Jiaqing named four after the rebuilding, in 1809 (虚受轩, 委宛藏, 碧静堂, 菱香沜; E0104).

CC05.what_en: 得全阁 Dequan Ge, south-west of 思永斋 beyond the stream: 得全阁 (plaque 天心水面) with 宝云楼 to the south and 远风楼 to the north (S05 j83:10b-11a; E0145); S361 has three waterside towers facing east, the main one of three bays with double eaves, and two nine-arch bent timber bridges (E0146). Finished 1747; poems 1758-64 (E0140-E0144).
CC05.survives_en: Service buildings on the site in about 2011 (E1011); two lakeside photographs tie to it only as a guess (P0472, P0473).

CC07.what_en: 流香渚 Liuxiang Zhu, a pavilion west of 海岳开襟 beyond the water, with 罨画溪 to its north; a path west from here reaches 明春门 of 圆明园 (S05 j83:11b-12a; E0166). Of 1747 with 海岳开襟 (E0164). A modern 3D model of the pavilion is R0100.
CC07.survives_en: Service buildings on the site in about 2011 (E1011); a 3D model of the pavilion by the park's company (R0100).

CC12.what_en: 丛芳榭 Congfang Xie, east of 平畴交远风, with 琴清斋 behind it (S05 j83:12b-13a; E0199): of 1747, a five-bay hall on the lake with the pavilions 漾月 and 集虚, the west half of the later 狮子林 group (E0223). Qianlong's poem of 1759 gives a curved gallery, an open hall and steps down to the pool (E0196).

CC17.what_en: 东宫门 Dong Gongmen (大东门), the east gate of Changchun Yuan, reached from 鉴园 by a hill path: a seven-bay gate of two floors facing east, three-bay court rooms north and south, a moat with a stone bridge outside (S05 j83:18a; E0334, E0391). Jiaqing set out from it for the north in 1815-1820 (E0331-E0333). Malone repeats hearsay that Xianfeng left by it for Jehol in 1860 and that Cixi rebuilt it (E0392).
CC17.survives_en: Malone (1934) reports stone lions and the bridge at the east gate (E0335, E0392). No dig of the east gate found; the 2001-04 gate-quarter report (S316) covers the south gate, not this one.

QC04.what_en: 敷春堂 Fuchun Tang, "Hall of Spreading Spring", was the residence block at the centre of Qichun Yuan, on the axis from the great gate in the south-east: 迎晖殿 (勤政殿 under Jiaqing), 中和堂, 敷春堂, up to 问月楼 on the lake shore (E0524, E0572, E0567). Begun 1801 north of 迎晖殿 (E0588): a five-bay 工字 hall with 集禧堂 before it and the five-bay, two-storey 问月楼 behind; 凌虚阁 east of the rear hall, the small chapel 翠合轩, 澄光榭 south-east of 问月楼, 蔚藻堂 in a court (E0588). In 1808 Jiaqing had a south-facing gate with offices, screen wall and barriers built on the model of the Changchun Yuan gate (E0566). From 1821-22 Daoguang made Qichun Yuan the empress dowager's garden instead of repairing 畅春园, with a dividing wall from 四宜书屋 to the west wall of 正觉寺 (E0426); 敷春堂 was the dowager's residence under Daoguang and Xianfeng (E0586, E0590), housing the dowager 康慈 from 1852 (E0625). It is one of the four season halls of Jiaqing's garden, with 清夏斋, 涵秋馆 and 生冬室 (E0661). It burned on 18 October 1860 (E0680); only 18 bays of duty rooms, kitchens and a pharmacy survived (E0586).
QC04.scene_en: Not in the Forty Scenes. Jiaqing's 绮春园三十景, listed in 养吉斋丛录 with Daoguang's colophon, open with 敷春堂 and include five more parts of this block: 鉴德书屋, 翠合轩, 凌虚阁, 澄光榭 and 问月楼, and 蔚藻堂 (S223 卷十八 leaf 4: 三十景者：敷春堂　鑑德書屋　翠合軒　凌虛閣 ... 澄光榭　問月樓 ... 蔚藻堂; E0448). The same text names 迎晖殿 as the main hall of the dowager's residence under Daoguang (E0448).
QC04.later_en: Dated plans: 1838 (heated beds added in the hall, 样084-7-1; E0591, E0592), 24th of the 8th month of Daoguang 30 (1850, Tsinghua PpXXI11-7: 颐寿轩, 敷春堂, east and west 所, kitchen, pharmacy; E0578, E0593), and winter 1859-60, the last before the destruction (样088-6-1; E0594, E0595). The claim that Daoguang renamed it 永春堂 (E0587) is not borne out: 1832, 1856 and 1873 documents still write 敷春堂 (E0585, E0381, E0434). In 1873 Tongzhi's project renamed it 天地一家春 and drew a new hall on its site (E0434, E0596, E0597): after the target state.
QC04.survives_en: Service buildings stood on the site in about 2011 (E1011). Ruin photographs of a broken stone bridge are tied to it as likely (P0460-P0463). No dig found.
QC04.gaps_en: Four dated Yangshi Lei plans (1838, 1850, 1859-60, and the 1873 project) exist but none is viewed: the 1859-60 sheet 样088-6-1 is the best single target for the 1860 state of any Qichun compound. No sizes beyond S01.

QC08.what_en: 鉴碧亭 Jianbi Ting, "Pavilion of the Green Mirror", a square pavilion in the middle of a lake west of 迎晖殿, reached by boat, with 正觉寺 to its west (E0675, E0676). Begun in mid-Jiaqing: a double-eaved square pavilion, three bays a side, with a gallery round it; on the north of the islet the five-bay 天心水面 with annexes and the pavilion 玩鹤; a single-arch stone bridge divided inner and outer water (E0676, E0675). Jiaqing's seven poems run 1811-1820 (E0675). Burned in October 1860 (E0680).
QC08.survives_en: Rebuilt on its site (E0569) and photographed 2012-2026 (P0421, P0422, P0423); the stone arch bridge P0424. A 2007 survey north of 鉴碧亭 found an island edged with stone and three rock piles, 43-86 by 12-81 m, 5872 m2 (E0791); a 2009 survey covered the lake between 正觉寺, 鉴碧亭 and 湛清轩 (E0686, E0687). Rebuilding: Tsinghua's rehabilitation paper R0303.

QC07.what_en: 涵秋馆 Hanqiu Guan, "Hall Holding Autumn", on a long north-south island north-west of 敷春堂, about 200 by 60 m, with lake to the east and north, facing 凤麟洲 to the east, planted for autumn colour (E0663, E0660). Begun early in Jiaqing's reign (about 1805, added 1810): a south-facing seven-bay double 工字 hall, front and rear halls with galleries, and a rockwork fountain between them fed by a raised tank east of the wall (E0660, E0661, E0662). The 'autumn' of the four season halls (E0661). Near it stood 仙人承露台, a bronze immortal on a high platform, whose base is now in 中山公园 (E0662). Burned on 18 October 1860 (E0680).
QC07.survives_en: A 2007 survey west of 仙人承露台 covered about 2,586 m2 (55-74 by 26-48 m) with two stone stairs on the north and west (E0664, E0665); results paywalled. Service buildings stood on it about 2011 (E1011).

QC05.what_en: 清夏斋 Qingxia Zhai, "Studio of Clear Summer", in the west of Qichun Yuan, two courts side by side on land with a long history: 裕亲王's 萼辉园 about 1687, then 交辉园, 春和园, and Prince Cheng's 西爽村 from 1773 to 1799 (E0626). West is 清夏斋, a seven-bay 工字 hall (palace_r7_halls; E0517, E0626); east is 延寿寺 (first 双寿寺, renamed 竹林院 by Jiaqing), front hall three bays, rear five (E0626). Jiaqing noted in 1804 that the old plaque here read 凤麟洲, given by Qianlong to Prince Cheng, before that name moved to the island QC06 (E0606). Poems of 1805-1824 show a study on a green pool with a stream, rocks, a small cascade, pines and bamboo, used in summer (E0624). A wine-cup pavilion (流杯亭) stood in it: square, 12 square column bases, about 48 stones, throne in the south half, cup stone in the north (E0628, E0629). From 1850 (or 1855, E0625) the residence of 如皇贵太妃 until her death in spring 1860 (E0624, E0625). Burned on 18 October 1860 (E0680).
QC05.scene_en: In Jiaqing's 绮春园三十景: 清夏斋 and 竹林院 (the east court, later 延寿寺) (S223 卷十八; E0448). The same text says the few bays once named 凤麐洲 were renamed 清夏斋: 舊有數楹名鳳麐洲，後易名清夏齋 (S223; E0448), which agrees with Jiaqing's note of 1804 (E0606).
QC05.later_en: Renamed 清夏堂 in Tongzhi's edict of 1873 (E0434); six card models of the 1874 design survive in the Palace Museum (E0627): both after the target state, so they show the 1874 project, not 1860.
QC05.survives_en: In about 2011 the sites of 清夏堂 (清夏斋) and 延寿寺 were occupied by other institutions (E1011). The stone seat of the wine-cup pavilion is said to survive (E0629).

QC11.what_en: 正觉寺 Zhengjue Si, "Temple of Perfect Enlightenment", stands on the west side of 绮春园 Qichun Yuan, outside the garden wall but linked to it by a back gate (S228). It was completed in 1773 (乾隆三十八年) as a Tibetan Buddhist temple (S228; E0506; E0683 gives 1773-74), served by a 达喇嘛 and 40 lamas sent from 宝谛寺 Baodi Si (E0683); it was the only temple of the three gardens run by lamas (E0681). It faces south with five buildings on the axis: a three-bay gate with Qianlong's plaque in four scripts, bell and drum towers, the five-bay 天王殿 Tianwang Dian, the seven-bay 三圣殿 Sansheng Dian on a stone terrace, the 文殊亭 Wenshu Ting, and the seven-bay 最上楼 Zuishang Lou; a monks' yard of 8 buildings and 22 bays lay on the east (E0681). Other names are reported: 正觉殿 for 三圣殿 and 殊像阁 for 文殊亭 (E0682, E0684, both from search extracts). When British troops burned 绮春园 on 18 October 1860, 正觉寺 was spared, as were 惠济祠 and 河神庙 (E0680; E0451); it also came through 1900 (S228; E0679).
QC11.survives_en: In the early Republic it was bought by 颜惠庆 Yan Huiqing as a private villa (images removed, lamas dismissed), then sold to Tsinghua as staff housing; 三圣殿 was gone by 1933; most buildings still stood in the 1960s, and from the 1970s three district factories occupied the site (S228; E0679). Before the restoration only the gate, the 文殊亭, four side halls and 26 old trees remained; 天王殿, 三圣殿, the west 金刚殿 and the seven-bay rear tower 最上楼 were wholly or partly destroyed (S228). Phase 1, finished in October 2003, repaired 990 m2 of old buildings: the gate, 文殊亭, the east and west 五佛殿, the east and west side halls and the west corner rooms; phase 2, begun on 16 December 2009, rebuilt 2,659 m2: 天王殿, 三圣殿, 最上楼, the 六大金刚殿, the east corner rooms, side gates and service buildings; the temple opened on trial on 6 July 2011 (S228; E0679). The column bases, Sumeru base and lower wall bricks of 三圣殿 are Qing remains (S228). So the period fabric is the gate, 文殊亭, the four side halls (the 五佛殿 pair and the side-hall pair) and the west corner rooms, with the Qing base and lower walls of 三圣殿; 天王殿, 三圣殿 and 最上楼 seen today are rebuilds of 2009-11 (S228; P0428, P0429, P0431). S228 does not say whether the bell and drum towers are old or new. Site 14,300 m2, buildings 3,649 m2 (S228). A salvage dig of 2005 in front of the gate found a road base, a carriageway and house remains over about 300 m2 (E0685); a dig report on 天王殿 is known by title only (S315, E0688). Pre-restoration photographs: Sirén's view of 三圣殿 (P0177, 1918-35 by Commons, so before 1933 if the hall is the 三圣殿) and a Bundesarchiv view dated 1900 on Commons that probably shows 文殊亭 and 最上楼 (P0173).
QC11.best_en: P0177 (Sirén, 1918-35) is the only picture on disk of the lost 三圣殿 before demolition; P0173 probably shows the double-eaved octagonal 文殊亭 and the two-storey 最上楼 with its balcony, about 1900 by the Commons date. The 2013 photographs (P0427-P0431) show the restored and rebuilt temple: good for the surviving halls, not for 三圣殿.
QC11.gaps_en: No measured plan of the temple is on disk; the park's restoration survey of 2002-11 is not published here. S228 says the rebuild drew on photographs of the gate, a Yangshi Lei ground plan (样式雷地盘看样图) and Qing temples of the same type such as 普宁寺 at Chengde; that plan is not seen. The interior-fitting sheet of 正觉殿 (E0684) and the 天王殿 dig report (E0688) are titles only. R0005 (圆明园正觉寺建筑研究) may carry the survey figures: not seen.
QC11.what_zh: 正觉寺位于绮春园西侧，在园墙之外，以后门与绮春园相通（S228）。乾隆三十八年（1773）建成，为藏传佛教寺庙（S228; E0506），由宝谛寺派驻达喇嘛及喇嘛四十名（E0683），是圆明三园中唯一由喇嘛住持的寺庙（E0681）。寺坐北朝南，中轴线上依次为三间山门（乾隆御书满、汉、蒙、藏四体寺额）、钟鼓楼、五间天王殿、建于石台上的七间三圣殿、文殊亭和七间最上楼；东侧有僧房八座二十二间（E0681; S228）。1860年10月18日英军焚烧绮春园时，正觉寺与惠济祠、河神庙得以幸免（E0680）；1900年亦未受损（S228）。
QC11.survives_zh: 民国初年，正觉寺被颜惠庆购为私人别墅，佛像被拆除，喇嘛被遣散，后又转售清华大学作教职员宿舍；1933年时三圣殿已不存（S228）。20世纪70年代起三家区属企业进驻，至修复前寺内仅存山门、文殊亭、四座配殿及26株古树，天王殿、三圣殿、西侧金刚殿和七间后楼最上楼已全部或部分损毁（S228）。2003年一期工程修缮原有建筑990平方米；2009年12月16日二期工程开工，复建天王殿、三圣殿、最上楼、六大金刚殿等2659平方米；2011年7月6日试开放（S228）。三圣殿的柱础、须弥座和腰线以下墙砖为清代原物（S228）。因此，今天所见的山门、文殊亭和配殿为原有建筑，天王殿、三圣殿和最上楼为2009年至2011年复建（S228）。
QC11.summary_en: The lama temple of 1773 on the west side of Qichun Yuan, the one group of the three gardens that came through 1860 and 1900. Damaged in the 20th century, it was repaired in 2003 and its lost main halls rebuilt in 2009-11.
QC11.summary_zh: 绮春园西侧的喇嘛寺，建成于1773年，是圆明三园中唯一躲过1860年和1900年两次劫难的建筑群；20世纪遭到破坏，2003年修缮，2009年至2011年复建了已毁的主要殿宇。

QC01.what_en: 绮春园宫门 Qichun Yuan Gongmen, the main gate in the south of Qichun Yuan. Jiaqing ordered in 1808 a south-facing gate with offices, a screen wall and barriers on the model of the Changchun Yuan gate (E0566); it was built in 1809 and called the new gate (新宫门) (E0568, E0497). The gate quarter, from the screen wall to the hill behind 中和堂, measures about 200 by 120 m; the great and second gates are gate halls with rolled-ridge hip-and-gable roofs (E0568). It burned in October 1860 (E0680; E0497 lists the gate district among survivors, unverified). Malone's plate shows a gate rebuilt after 1860 by the empress dowager and the garden renamed 万春园 (E0492).
QC01.survives_en: The gates and walls were rebuilt on their sites in 1986 (E0568, S227) and serve as the park's south entrance (P0418, P0419, P0466, P0467): a modern rebuild, not the gate of 1860.

QC02.what_en: 迎晖殿 Yinghui Dian, "Hall Welcoming the Sunlight", the main hall inside the south gate of Qichun Yuan, called 勤政殿 under Jiaqing and begun in 1809 (E0572, E0567). North of it is the seven-bay 中和堂, then the path past the hill to the dowager's quarter at 敷春堂 (E0572, E0524). Under Daoguang the dowager received birthday homage here (E0568, E0572); it is named as the main hall of the dowager's residence (S223; E0448), and the coffin of the dowager 康慈 lay here in 1855 (E0625). Burned in October 1860 (E0680). The terrace remains; the gate in front was rebuilt in 1986 (E0568).
QC02.survives_en: The park page of 2011 says the terrace of 迎晖殿 remains while the gates in front were rebuilt in 1986 (E0568); the status table of about 2011 lists 迎晖殿 among the rebuilt sites (E0569). One ruin photograph of a broken bridge is tied to it as likely (P0420).

QC17.what_en: 春泽斋 Chunze Zhai, "Studio of Spring Moisture", built in mid-Jiaqing west of 展诗应律: a seven-bay hall with front and rear annexes, and 水心榭, a three-bay open hall on the pool; east of it courts with 畅惠轩, 蘋香沜, 茂悦精舍 and 惠圃; across the pool the three-bay 时登楼 (E0749). Jiaqing's seven poems (1802-1819) are about rain and the wheat and say nearly nothing on its form (E0748). Burned on 18 October 1860 (E0680). No picture, dig or plan on disk.
QC17.scene_en: In Jiaqing's 绮春园三十景: 春泽斋 and 水心榭 (S223 卷十八; E0448).

QC12.what_en: 澄心堂 Chengxin Tang, on an island in the south lake of the western group of Qichun Yuan, once the waste plot 竹园: rebuilt about 1815 as a five-bay hall in two rolls with a hip-gable annex and side wings, stone-edged banks and bridges, with plaques 垂虹榭 and 绮旭轩 (E0696, E0698). Xianfeng served the dowager consort a meal here in 1852 (E0697).
QC12.survives_en: Occupied by another institution in about 2011 (E1011). No dig found.

QC13.what_en: 含晖楼 Hanhui Lou, in the south-west of Qichun Yuan on the site of the old 含晖园 (given to Prince Yongxuan about 1773, to Princess Zhuangjing 1801, returned 1811 as 南园), when the tower 联辉楼 was moved here from 西爽村: a two-storey tower of seven bays with a riding track (撒马道) and lawn in front for mounted archery (E0722, E0705, E0718, E0720). The Thirty Scenes call it 含光楼, 'the old 联辉楼' (S223; E0448). Daoguang held lantern viewing and banquets here with the dowager (E0719, E1186); the emperor passed it in 1856 (E1524).
QC13.scene_en: In Jiaqing's 绮春园三十景 as 含光楼, 'the old 联辉楼' (S223 卷十八: 含光樓（即舊時聯暉樓）; E0448, E0701).
QC13.survives_en: Occupied by another institution in about 2011 (E1011). No dig found.

QC14.what_en: 畅和堂 Changhe Tang, in the south-west corner by the Hanlin garden 澄怀园, on the site of Ertai's 晚香园 (from 1732) and Yin Jishan's 寻春园, derelict after 1770 and rebuilt in 1813: a three-bay gate 松路花龛 and a five-bay main hall in two rolls with side halls, among them 澄霞宇 (E0728). Jiaqing's poems are of 1814 (E0723-E0730).

QC19.what_en: 四宜书屋 Siyi Shuwu of Qichun Yuan (not the Yuanming Yuan scene of the same name), built 1805 west of 生冬室 across the long river, in the 绮春园三十景 (S223; E0448, E0590, E0760). A gate of three bays and two halls of five (palace_r7_halls). In 1822 the dividing wall of the dowager's garden ran along its west and north walls (E0426); in 1855 a stone wall and corner gate were added for Daoguang's widows (E0625). A Yangshi Lei survey plan of 1850 exists (E0766); a survey of 2009 on the north bank of 湛清轩 found rubble to 0.6 m over Qing layers to 1.6 m (E0767, E0768).
QC19.scene_en: In Jiaqing's 绮春园三十景 (S223 卷十八; E0448), with a poem of 1805 (E0760).

QC06.what_en: 凤麟洲 Fenglin Zhou, two islands in the east part of the large northern water of Qichun Yuan, joined by a winding bridge, begun 1807: a seven-bay main hall in two rolls with a five-bay front annex, the open hall 绣漪轩 before it, a side court east and a service court on the small east island (E0649, E0651, E0524). The name first belonged to the studio later called 清夏斋 (E0606; S223). Jiaqing's poems from 1806 tell of an old pool re-dug, winding galleries, a pine crag and a rainbow bridge (E0648). A 2007 survey found area A about 50 by 26-48 m (1,690 m2) and area B 24 by 22 m (445 m2), all stone-edged (E0652, E0653).
QC06.survives_en: Service buildings stood on it in about 2011 (E1011); surveyed in 2007 before a conservation project (E0652); ruin photographs of 2012-13 (P0436, P0437, P0454, P0502).
